https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-neu.summary: When young Dr. Thomas Karikari entered his laboratory in Sweden years ago for his research program, one question lingered on his mind: “Why don’t we have a good blood test kit for Alzheimer’s dementia?” This was a question that not only developed into a hypothesis for research, but one that was ready to transform biomedical research in neuroscience and enhance medical care for people living with the condition.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-neu.summary_zh: 多年前，年轻的Thomas Karikari博士在瑞典进入实验室开展研究项目时，脑海中始终萦绕着一个问题：“为什么我们没有一种适用于阿尔茨海默痴呆症的良好血液检测套件？”这个问题不仅逐渐发展为一项研究假设，也已具备改变神经科学生物医学研究、改善患者医疗照护的潜力。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-neu.body: When young Dr. Thomas Karikari entered his laboratory in Sweden years ago for his research program, one question lingered on his mind: “Why don’t we have a good blood test kit for Alzheimer’s dementia?” This was a question that not only developed into a hypothesis for research, but one that was ready to transform biomedical research in neuroscience and enhance medical care for people living with the condition. Many scientists had attempted in their might to understand how the disease could be easily tested without an invasive procedure, but failed at it. Dr. Karikari was nearly discouraged in his quest for answers. “I was told you don’t talk about it. Companies have spent millions; they couldn’t do it. People have spent years, but they couldn’t do it. So, just shut up,” he recounted. But, burning with the desire, the neuroscientist was poised to develop his question into a groundbreaking practical solution to testing the neurological disorder with blood samples. ‘And I set out to do it as my side project. I wasn’t even doing it as my main project because no one believed it would work,” he noted. For decades, diagnosing Alzheimer’s required invasive procedures such as spinal taps or expensive brain scans. These tests are often inaccessible in many regions of the world, especially in low-resource communities. Dr. Karikari’s experience with limited diagnostic capacity in Ghana fueled the need for a solution. So, when he was headhunted to lead a clinical research program in diagnostic medicine at the University of Pittsburgh in the United States of America (USA), he was bent on dedicating most of his career to developing, improving, and validating the clinical performance of blood tests that could simplify Alzheimer’s diagnosis. After grueling years and sleepless nights at the lab, he finally found a means to detect the disease. Dr. Karikari has about 300 publications to his name. He has published multiple seminal works in leading medical journals describing major innovations in high-performance blood tests for the neurological disorder. He also holds several patents and pending patents to that effect. Last year, Dr. Karikari was recognized by Clarivate as among the top 1% of scientists worldwide. The high-impact journal Nature also named him as a Rising Star in Ageing research, an accolade that was bestowed on only three investigators. These accomplishments have earned Dr. Karikari global respect and recognition as a leading figure in biomedical research. His achievements were celebrated at the just-ended Millennium Excellence Awards USA, spearheaded by the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II. “I am so proud that today I have made that contribution. A contribution that would change the face of how we treat diseases for a long time. This is just a stepping stone,” he gladly noted. Dr. Thomas Karikari's groundbreaking research has led to the development of multiple blood tests for Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia. In his acceptance speech, Dr. Karikari further noted that two new blood tests for Alzheimer’s disease have been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). This adds to two already approved by the authority over the last two years. Dr. Karikari’s mission is beyond scientific discovery—he wants diagnostics to reach everyone, including people in places like his home village of Manfo. He says a parcel of land has been acquired back home in his late mother’s hometown of Achinakrom near Ejisu in the Ashanti region to continue with the groundbreaking scientific discoveries in Ghana. He is poised to establish a research center to help advance biomedical research on the continent

https://www.myjoyonline.com/ghanaian-neu.body_zh: 多年前，年轻的 Thomas Karikari 博士在瑞典进入自己的实验室开展研究项目时，一个问题始终萦绕在他脑海中：“为什么我们没有一种适用于阿尔茨海默型痴呆的良好血液检测工具？”这个问题不仅发展成一项研究假设，也已准备好彻底改变神经科学领域的生物医学研究，并改善患者的医疗护理。许多科学家曾竭尽全力探索如何无需侵入性操作便可轻松检测这种疾病，但均未能成功。Karikari 博士在寻求答案的过程中几乎要灰心放弃。他回忆道：“有人告诉我，不要谈这件事。各家公司投入了数百万美元，却没能做到。人们花了数年时间，也没能做到。所以，闭嘴吧。”然而，这名神经科学家的求知欲熊熊燃烧，他已准备好将这个问题转化为一种开创性的实用解决方案，利用血液样本检测这一神经系统疾病。他指出：“我着手把它当作自己的副业项目来完成。我甚至没有把它作为主要项目，因为没人相信它会奏效。”数十年来，诊断阿尔茨海默病需要依靠脊髓穿刺等侵入性操作或费用高昂的脑部扫描。在世界许多地区，尤其是资源有限的社区，这类检测往往无法获得。Karikari 博士在加纳亲身经历诊断能力有限的状况，进一步推动了寻找解决方案的需求。因此，当他受邀前往美国匹兹堡大学领导诊断医学领域的一项临床研究项目时，他决心将职业生涯的大部分时间投入开发、改进并验证血液检测的临床性能，以简化阿尔茨海默病的诊断。经过在实验室里多年埋头钻研和无数个不眠之夜，他终于找到了一种检测这种疾病的方法。Karikari 博士名下约有 300 篇论文。他在顶级医学期刊上发表过多篇开创性著作，介绍在这一神经系统疾病的高性能血液检测方面取得的重要创新。他还持有多项相关专利，另有多项专利申请正在审理中。去年，Clarivate 表彰 Karikari 博士位列全球顶尖 1% 的科学家之列。高影响力期刊 Nature 还将他评为老龄化研究领域的新星，这项荣誉仅授予 3 名研究人员。这些成就使 Karikari 博士赢得了全球尊重，并被公认为生物医学研究领域的领军人物。他的成果在刚刚举行的 Millennium Excellence Awards USA 上受到庆祝，该活动由阿散蒂王 Otumfuo Osei Tutu II 领衔主办。他欣喜地表示：“我非常自豪，今天我作出了这份贡献。这份贡献将长久改变我们治疗疾病的方式。这只是一个里程碑。”Thomas Karikari 博士的开创性研究推动了多种阿尔茨海默病及其他类型痴呆症血液检测方法的开发。在获奖感言中，Karikari 博士进一步指出，已有 2 项用于阿尔茨海默病的新型血液检测获得美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准。加上此前两年已获该机构批准的 2 项血液检测，目前共有 4 项获得批准。Karikari 博士的使命不止于科学发现——他希望诊断技术惠及每一个人，包括他家乡 Manfo 村等地的人们。他说，已在阿散蒂地区 Ejisu 附近、已故母亲的故乡 Achinakrom 购得一块土地，以便继续在加纳推进这些开创性的科学发现。他正准备建立一座研究中心，帮助推动非洲大陆的生物医学研究

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian interventions following a deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, which reportedly left between 57 and 60 people dead. The lawmakers also urged the federal government to complete the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project to improve security operations and enable the rapid deployment of security personnel to affected communities. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Mohammed Audu (APC, Taraba) during Thursday’s plenary. Presenting the motion, Mr Audu said the attack occurred on 23 October when traders and residents gathered at the community market. He said the attackers opened fire, killing 10 people at the scene, while the ensuing panic caused several people to jump into a river, bringing the reported death toll to between 57 and 60. According to the lawmaker, the attackers allegedly came from forested areas in Plateau State, including Dutsen Zaki in Wase Local Government Area, Kukawa in Kanam Local Government Area and areas around the Yankari Game Reserve and Gwana Mountain in Alkaleri Local Government Area of Bauchi State. He said these areas shared boundaries with communities in Karim Lamido, making improved road access and coordinated security operations necessary to prevent further attacks. Mr Audu described the incident as unprecedented in its scale in Karim Lamido, adding that the affected communities had suffered considerably because of the lack of access roads. “This type of deadly attack has never taken place in Karim Lamido Local Government; the people of Karim Lamido have suffered a lot. No access road leading to all these areas,” he said. He also reported another attack on 26 October in neighbouring Gomben Dela community, where the assailants allegedly looted food items and seized vehicles. No deaths were reported in the second incident. The lawmaker asked the House to observe a minute of silence for those killed in Binnari and neighbouring villages. He further urged the federal government to strengthen intelligence sharing among security agencies in Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to prevent a recurrence. Mr Audu also called on the North-East Development Commission (NEDC), the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons and other humanitarian agencies to provide relief materials to affected communities. He listed building materials, food, blankets, mattresses and mats among the items needed to support survivors and affected families. The motion also commended the Taraba State Governor, security commanders and other security agencies for their response to the attack. Contributing to the debate, the Minority Leader, Fred Agbedi, expressed concern over the recurring attacks on communities across the country, questioning whether the government was doing enough to protect lives and property. He said the House had repeatedly been confronted with reports of killings and destruction of property, often followed by motions and minutes of silence. “I remember that in 2016, on this same floor, I rose to say that the life of a Nigerian is just now worth a one-minute silence,” Mr Agbedi said. He acknowledged the efforts of security personnel but argued that the scale of the attacks demanded a stronger response, particularly through the deployment of modern technology. According to him, attackers often invade communities, carry out killings and leave before security agencies respond. “The situation where criminals will go to a community, attack the community, and there is no response. They finish. They will leave, and then we start reacting. It’s like medicine after death,” he said. Mr Agbedi questioned whether the country had adequately deployed technological tools to identify attackers and trace their movements. He also raised concerns about the funding and implementation of security budgets, urging relevant House committees to move beyond resolutions and take practical steps to improve national security. He said lawmakers serving on security-related committees had a responsibility to work closely with security agencies and ensure that the necessary measures were implemented to protect Nigerians. Another Taraba lawmaker, Jaafaru Yakubu, said the state and neighbouring areas had experienced coordinated criminal activities, including banditry and kidnapping. Mr Yakubu said the Binnari attack was followed by another assault in which the attackers allegedly took food items and destroyed facilities belonging to the federal government. Presiding over the plenary, Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu acknowledged the concerns raised by Mr Agbedi but defended the federal government’s efforts to tackle insecurity. Mr Kalu said the House’s resolutions had contributed to measures taken by the government and that the legislature should not be seen as merely holding sessions without achieving results. He cited figures he attributed to government reports, including more than 13,000 terrorists reportedly killed in the preceding year and an 81 per cent reduction in violent deaths since 2023. He also said more than 124,000 fighters and their family members had surrendered since 2023, while over 104,000 people had been processed through the Safe Corridor programme in collaboration with the Multinational Joint Task Force. The deputy speaker further said the number of local government areas under insurgent control had declined from 17 in 2022 to six, citing data from 2025. On weapons recovery, he said more than 19,000 illegal weapons had been destroyed. Mr Kalu also highlighted an increase in security spending, saying the allocation rose from ₦2.98 trillion in 2023 to ₦3.25 trillion in 2024, ₦4.91 trillion in 2025 and ₦5.4 trillion in 2026. He added that the government had recruited 30,000 additional police personnel and expanded electronic policing initiatives. The deputy speaker said the figures demonstrated that the government was acting on the legislature’s interventions and that security operations were producing results. He maintained that the minute of silence was intended to honour victims, while the government continued efforts to reduce insecurity. “Your resolutions here, your motions here, do not end only with one minute silence. The one-minute silence is to honor those who have lost their life, but the number is shrinking by the day because the government is deliberate in making sure that the issue of insecurity is reduced, and we must give kudos to whom kudos is due. This administration has been doing tremendously well,” he said. The House subsequently adopted the motion through a voice vote and observed a minute of silence in honour of those killed in the attacks. Mr Kalu referred the matter to the House Committees on the North-East Development Commission, Works and NEMA for further legislative action. The referral to the works committee is expected to facilitate consideration of the abandoned Wase-Karim Lamido road project, which the lawmakers said would improve access for security personnel responding to emergencies. The committees are expected to pursue the House’s resolutions on road access, emergency response and assistance to communities affected by the attacks
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 武装分子袭击：众议员要求在塔拉巴采取安全和 humanitarian 干预措施
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh:
众议院呼吁在塔拉巴州卡里姆·拉米多地方政府辖区比纳里社区发生致命土匪袭击后紧急采取安全和 Humanitarian 干预措施。据报道，袭击造成57至60人死亡。议员们还敦促联邦政府完成被搁置的瓦塞—卡里姆·拉米多公路项目，以改善安全行动并使安全人员能够迅速部署到受影响社区。

这些决议是在周四全体会议上根据穆罕默德·奥杜（APC，塔拉巴州）提出的紧急公共重要性动议作出的。奥杜先生提出动议时表示，袭击发生于10月23日，当时商贩和居民聚集在社区市场。袭击者开枪，当场杀死10人，随后引发的恐慌导致多人跳入河中，使据报死亡人数升至57至60人。

据这位议员说，袭击者据称来自普拉托州的林地地区，包括瓦塞地方政府辖区的杜岑扎基、卡纳姆地方政府辖区的库卡瓦，以及包奇州阿尔卡莱里地方政府辖区扬卡里禁猎区和格瓦纳山周边地区。他说，这些地区与卡里姆·拉米多的社区接壤，因此有必要改善道路通行条件并协调安全行动，以防止再次发生袭击。

奥杜先生称，这次事件的规模在卡里姆·拉米多前所未有，并表示由于缺乏通行道路，受影响社区一直遭受严重困苦。他说：“卡里姆·拉米多地方政府从未发生过这种致命袭击；卡里姆·拉米多人民受苦良多。所有这些地区都没有通往那里的通行道路。”

他还报告说，邻近的贡本德拉社区于10月26日也遭到袭击，袭击者据称抢走食品并夺走车辆。第二起事件没有人员死亡报告。

议员请求众议院为在比纳里及邻近村庄遇难的民众默哀一分钟。他还敦促联邦政府加强塔拉巴州、普拉托州和包奇州各安全机构之间的情报共享，防止此类事件重演。奥杜先生还呼吁东北发展委员会（NEDC）、国家紧急事务管理局（NEMA）、国家难民、移民和境内流离失所者委员会及其他 Humanitarian 机构向受影响社区提供救援物资。他列举了建筑材料、食品、毛毯、床垫和垫子等所需物品，用于扶持幸存者和受影响家庭。

动议还赞扬塔拉巴州州长、安全部队指挥官及其他安全机构对袭击所作的应对。

 minority leader弗雷德·阿格贝迪参与讨论时，对全国多地社区反复遭袭表示担忧，质问政府是否采取了足够措施保护生命和财产。他说，众议院多次收到有关杀戮和财产破坏的报告，随后往往只能通过动议和默哀 minute 予以回应。阿格贝迪先生说：“我记得2016年，也是在这个议事厅里，我曾站起来说，一个尼日利亚人的生命如今只值一分钟的沉默。”

他认可安全人员的努力，但认为袭击规模要求采取更有力的应对措施，尤其是部署现代技术。据他所说，袭击者经常闯入社区，实施杀戮，然后在安全机构作出反应前离开。他说：“罪犯来到一个社区，袭击这个社区，却得不到任何回应。他们得手后离开，我们才开始反应。这就像人死后才用药。”

阿格贝迪先生质问，国家是否已充分部署技术工具来识别袭击者并追踪其行踪。他还担忧安全预算的资金保障和落实情况，敦促众议院相关委员会不要止步于通过决议，而应采取切实措施改善国家安全。他说，担任安全相关委员会成员的议员有责任与安全机构密切合作，确保落实必要措施，保护尼日利亚人。

塔拉巴州另一名议员贾法鲁·雅库布表示，该州及邻近地区一直发生有组织的犯罪活动，包括土匪绑架和劫持。雅库布先生说，比纳里袭击之后又发生了一次袭击，袭击者据称拿走食品并摧毁联邦政府所属设施。

主持全体会议的副议长本杰明·卡卢承认了阿格贝迪先生提出的担忧，但为联邦政府打击不安全局势的努力辩护。卡卢先生说，众议会的决议推动政府采取了相关措施，立法机构不应被视为只是开会而没有取得成果。他援引据称来自政府报告的数据，包括前一年据报击毙逾13,000名恐怖分子，以及自2023年以来暴力死亡人数下降81%。

他还表示，自2023年以来，已有逾124,000名武装人员及其家属投降，另有逾104,000人通过与多国联合特遣部队合作开展的安全通道计划接受处置。副议长进一步援引2025年的数据称，处于叛乱分子控制下的地方政府辖区数量已从2022年的17个降至6个。在缴获武器方面，他说已有逾19,000件非法武器被销毁。

卡卢先生还强调安全支出有所增加，拨款从2023年的₦2.98万亿增至2024年的₦3.25万亿、2025年的₦4.91万亿和2026年的₦5.4万亿。他补充说，政府增聘了30,000名警察人员，并扩大了电子警务行动。副议长表示，这些数据证明政府正在落实立法机构的干预，安全行动也取得了成果。他坚持认为，默哀一分钟是为了向受害者致敬，而政府仍在继续努力减少不安全局势。

他说：“你们在这里通过的决议、提出的动议，不能仅以一分钟沉默告终。这一分钟的沉默是为了纪念那些失去生命的人，但遇害人数正在逐日减少，因为政府决心设法减少不安全局势，我们也应该向应当受到赞扬的人致敬本届政府表现得非常出色。”

众议院随后以口头表决方式通过动议，并为在袭击中遇难者默哀一分钟。卡卢先生将此事移交众议院东北发展委员会、工程委员会和国家紧急事务管理局委员会采取进一步立法行动。

移交工程委员会预计将推动审议被搁置的瓦塞—卡里姆·拉米多公路项目。议员们表示，该项目将改善安全人员应对紧急情况的通行条件。各委员会预计将推进众议院关于道路通行、紧急响应以及援助受袭社区的决议。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/minerals-com.body: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mineral rights of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Owere Mines, insisting that the company persistently failed to meet its statutory financial obligations despite several opportunities to settle its debts. According to the Commission, the company accumulated approximately US$8.33 million in unpaid Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees on its mining leases as of April 2025, alongside US$49,928 owed on prospecting licences. Addressing a press conference, the Commission rejected allegations by Northern Ashanti Mines that the termination was carried out in bad faith, maintaining that the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources acted within his legal authority. The Commission explained that Owere Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010 but subsequently failed to fulfil its annual payment obligations under Section 24 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). It disclosed that the company had accumulated more than US$4 million in outstanding fees by May 2020, prompting the issuance of a notice to remedy the breach. Following the takeover of the company by BCM Investments, management proposed settling the debt in four instalments. However, the Commission said the company failed to honour the arrangement despite being given additional opportunities. By October 2022, the outstanding debt had risen to US$5.59 million, increasing to US$6.18 million by December of the same year. The Commission indicated that further notices issued in April 2025 revealed that the company's indebtedness had reached US$8.33 million in mining lease fees, excluding outstanding prospecting licence fees. Consequently, on April 7, 2026, the Commission recommended the termination of the company's mineral rights to the Lands Minister, citing persistent non-payment. The Minister subsequently approved the issuance of the termination notice. Responding to the company's challenge to the debt figures, the Commission insisted that its records showed Northern Ashanti Mines had paid only US$300,000 in two instalments, contrary to the company's claim of having paid US$1 million. "For a company that claims to have spent US$200,000,000 on the mine, what prevented it from paying the US$8,000,000 owed to the people of Ghana?" the Commission questioned. It further criticised the company's decision to pursue legal action against the Lands Minister, the Minerals Commission and the Attorney-General while simultaneously seeking public dialogue over the matter. The Commission maintained that the company should allow the courts to determine the dispute rather than engage in what it described as litigation through the media. It stressed that the termination of the mineral rights meant the affected concessions had reverted to the State, without cancelling the company's outstanding financial liabilities. The Commission consequently announced its intention to pursue the recovery of all outstanding payments owed by Northern Ashanti Mines. It also emphasised the State's responsibility to protect the affected mining assets from encroachment and other illegal activities, citing Section 70 of Act 703. The Commission reaffirmed that due process had been followed throughout the termination proceedings and insisted that no mining company, whether locally or foreign-owned, would be permitted to disregard its statutory obligations. "No one is above the law in this country. If you flout the laws, there are sanctions, and those sanctions will apply," the Commission stated. It reiterated its commitment to enforcing Ghana's mining laws without fear or favour, stressing that the country's mineral resources belong to the people and must be managed in accordance with the law
https://www.myjoyonline.com/minerals-com.title_zh: 矿产委员会为终止北部阿散蒂矿区因830万美元债务而享有的采矿权进行辩护
https://www.myjoyonline.com/minerals-com.body_zh: 矿产委员会为终止 Northern Ashanti Mines Limited（原名 Owere Mines）的矿产权利辩护，称尽管多次给予该公司清偿债务的机会，该公司仍持续未能履行法定财务义务。委员会表示，截至2025年4月，该公司的采矿租约已拖欠约8.33 million US$的年度矿产权利费（AMR），另有49,928 US$的勘探许可证欠款。在记者会上，委员会驳斥了 Northern Ashanti Mines 关于终止决定出于恶意的指控，坚持认为土地与自然资源部长是在其法定权限内行事。委员会解释称，Owere Mines 于2010年1月取得一项涵盖595个地籍区块的采矿租约，但此后未履行《2006年矿产与采矿法》（第703号法案）第24条规定的年度付款义务。委员会披露，截至2020年5月，该公司拖欠费用已超过4 million US$，因此发出了整改违约行为的通知。BCM Investments 接管公司后，管理层提议分四期清偿债务。然而，委员会表示，尽管后来又获得了额外机会，公司仍未履行该安排。截至2022年10月，未偿债务已增至5.59 million US$，同年12月又增至6.18 million US$。委员会指出，2025年4月发出的进一步通知显示，公司采矿租约欠款已达8.33 million US$，尚未计算未偿勘探许可证费用。因此，委员会于2026年4月7日以持续不付款为由，建议终止该公司的矿产权利，部长随后批准发出终止通知。针对公司对债务数字提出的异议，委员会坚持其记录显示，Northern Ashanti Mines 仅分两期支付了300,000 US$，与该公司声称已支付1 million US$的说法不符。委员会质问：“对于一家声称已在该矿场投入200,000,000 US$的公司，是什么阻碍它支付欠加纳人民的8,000,000 US$呢？”委员会还批评该公司一方面决定对土地与自然资源部长、矿产委员会和总检察长提起法律诉讼，另一方面又寻求就此事开展公开对话。委员会坚持认为，公司应让法院裁定争议，而不是采取其所称的“通过媒体进行诉讼”。委员会强调，终止矿产权利意味着相关特许采矿权已回归国家，但并未取消公司尚未偿清的财务债务。因此，委员会宣布打算追缴 Northern Ashanti Mines 欠付的全部款项。委员会还强调，国家有责任依据第703号法案第70条保护相关采矿资产，防止侵占及其他非法活动，并重申终止程序全程遵循了正当程序，坚持任何本地或外资采矿公司都不得无视其法定义务。委员会表示：“在这个国家，没有人可以凌驾于法律之上。如果违反法律，就会受到制裁，而且这些制裁必定会得到适用。”委员会再次承诺将无畏且不偏不倚地执行加纳的采矿法，强调该国的矿产资源属于人民，必须依法进行管理

https://leadership.ng/u-s-ponders-update.body: No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result by Chika Izuora 13 seconds ago in Business The U.S. Department of Transportation has put forward a new safety regulations for liquefied natural gas facilities, seeking to accelerate infrastructure development and reduce operating costs as American exporters prepare for another major expansion in global natural gas markets. The proposal, issued by the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), would modernize federal LNG safety requirements by incorporating standards developed by the National Fire Protection Association. The changes address facility location, engineering, construction, operations, and maintenance, with greater flexibility to adopt newer technologies. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy estimates that the updated framework could save LNG operators approximately $100 million annually while maintaining safety protections. The projected savings are an agency estimate, and the proposal has not yet become a final regulation. The initiative comes as the United States strengthens its position as the world’s largest LNG exporter. American export capacity is expected to increase by approximately 100 million metric tons annually by the end of the decade, supported by projects already under development and additional planned investments. Global LNG demand has also become more sensitive to geopolitical disruptions. Interruptions to Middle Eastern gas shipments associated with the conflict involving Iran have encouraged international buyers to evaluate alternative suppliers and diversify long-term procurement arrangements. U.S. LNG developers have responded with additional investment commitments. Projects representing more than 50 million metric tons of annual capacity have reached final investment decisions since the beginning of 2025. Major exporters, including Cheniere Energy and Venture Global, are pursuing additional development opportunities as federal policy places greater emphasis on expanding domestic energy infrastructure. However, regulatory modernization does not eliminate the financial or operational challenges associated with LNG construction. Developers must still secure Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approvals, complete environmental reviews, arrange financing, and address potential legal challenges. Pipeline connections, specialized equipment availability, construction costs, and long-term customer contracts also influence project schedules. Delfin LNG, which is developing a floating export facility, illustrates the importance of infrastructure safety approvals. Its associated pipeline has not received publicly confirmed PHMSA clearance to resume operations following an explosion earlier this year. Separately, FERC has proposed a streamlined authorization framework for certain modifications and expansions at existing LNG facilities, including activities that could qualify for automatic approval or shortened review periods. For energy investors, the combined regulatory initiatives could improve development visibility and reduce some costs, although their financial impact will depend on final requirements and individual project circumstances. Additional LNG export capacity could support demand for U.S. natural gas production, particularly from major producing regions connected to Gulf Coast terminals. Midstream operators, engineering companies, compression equipment manufacturers, and construction contractors could also benefit from continued infrastructure investment. At the same time, greater export demand may increase domestic natural gas price sensitivity to international markets, creating different implications for producers, utilities, and industrial consumers. Chika Izuora 13秒前发布于商业

美国运输部提出了一套液化天然气设施新安全法规，旨在加快基础设施建设并降低运营成本；随着美国出口商准备在全球天然气市场进一步大规模扩张，此举势在必行。

这项由管道和危险材料安全管理局（PHMSA）发布的提案，将把美国国家消防协会制定的标准纳入其中，以更新联邦液化天然气安全要求。修改内容涉及设施选址、工程设计、建设和运营维护，并让采用新技术获得更大灵活性。

交通部长肖恩·达菲估计，更新后的监管框架每年可为液化天然气运营商节省约1亿美元，同时继续保持安全防护。预计节省额是该机构的估算，提案尚未成为最终法规。

随着美国加强其作为全球最大液化天然气出口国的地位，此项举措适时出台。预计到本十年末，美国出口能力将每年增加约1亿立方米，支撑这一增长的是已在开发的项目以及计划追加的投资。

全球液化天然气需求对地缘政治中断也变得更加敏感。与伊朗有关联的冲突导致中东天然气运输中断，促使国际买家评估替代供应商，并使长期采购安排多元化。

美国液化天然气开发商已相应作出更多投资承诺。自2025年初以来，代表年产能超过5000万吨的项目均已作出最终投资决定。

随着联邦政策更加重视扩大国内能源基础设施，陈宁能源和Venture Global等主要出口商正在寻求更多开发机会。

不过，监管现代化并未消除液化天然气建设面临的财务和运营挑战。开发商仍须取得联邦能源管理委员会批准、完成环境审查、安排融资并处理潜在法律挑战。管道连接、专用设备供应、施工成本和长期客户合同也会影响项目进度。

正在开发浮式出口设施的Delfin LNG，凸显了基础设施安全审批的重要性。今年早些时候发生爆炸后，其配套管道尚未获得公开确认的PHMSA复运许可。

此外，联邦能源管理委员会已提议为现有液化天然气设施的部分改建和扩建建立简化审批框架，其中包括可能符合自动批准或缩短审查期限的活动。

对能源投资者而言，这些监管举措combined起来可能提高开发项目的确定性并降低部分成本，但其财务影响将取决于最终要求和各个项目的具体情况。

液化天然气出口能力扩大可支撑美国天然气生产需求，尤其是与墨西哥湾沿岸终端相连的主要产气区。中游运营商、工程公司、压缩设备制造商和建筑承包商也将从持续的基础设施投资中受益。

与此同时，出口需求增加可能提高美国国内天然气价格对国际市场的敏感度，从而对生产商、公用事业公司和工业消费者产生不同影响。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/co.body_zh: 韩国电力电缆制造商Gaon Cable周四表示，已与美国一家云服务公司敲定价值1200亿韩元（9000万美元）的电缆供应协议。Gaon Cable的美国制造子公司LS Cable USA（LSCUS）将在明年上半年之前向该客户供应一套中压配电电缆系统。公司在一份新闻稿中表示了这一点。一名公司官员说：“这笔订单将支持Gaon Cable扩大其在北美人工智能数据中心（AIDC）电力基础设施市场的布局。”他还表示，公司计划扩大生产并拓宽客户群。Gaon Cable由韩国领先的电线电缆制造商LS Cable & System持有81.62%的股份。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.summary_zh: 韩国金融当局周四表示，将密切监测美国中期选举对金融市场的影响；如市场出现剧烈波动，将立即采取应对措施。财政部长补充说：“我们还需要关注美国中期选举后美国国会的构成、在政治格局变化下华盛顿对外政策的调整及其对市场的影响。”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: Korean financial authorities said Thursday they will closely monitor the impact of the U.S. midterm elections on financial markets and take immediate countermeasures if necessary in the event of sharp market fluctuations. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il held discussions on the issue with Bank of Korea (BOK) Gov. Shin Hyun-song, Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon and Financial Supervisory Service Gov. Lee Chan-jin after the U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate steady overnight. The Fed decided to maintain the rate in the 3.75-4.00 percent range in a 10-2 vote. The decision left the gap between the key interest rates of Korea and the United States at up to 1 percentage point. "The decision appears to reflect the Fed's continued focus on stabilizing consumer prices while assessing the impact of September's rate hike and other economic indicators to determine its future policy direction," Lee said. Lee noted that earnings and investment outlooks for major technology firms, along with movements in global oil prices, are fueling volatility in financial markets at home and abroad. "We also need to monitor the composition of the U.S. Congress following the midterm elections, changes in Washington's external policies amid the shifting political landscape and their impact on markets," the finance minister added. Lee, however, said Korea's economic fundamentals remain sound, with its gross domestic product (GDP) advancing 1 percent on-quarter in the third quarter. The finance minister pointed out that the U.S. elections and fiscal instability in France may also adversely affect the government bond market, noting that Korea will work with relevant institutions to implement timely market stabilization measures, such as emergency bond buybacks, when necessary. Separately, Lee said he would also discuss with the participants ways to shorten the stock settlement cycle from the current T+2 system to T+1. "Shortening the settlement cycle is an important task as it can reduce related risks and improve the efficiency of fund management," Lee said, noting the government will gather opinions on the matter from market participants. The BOK, meanwhile, said it will continue to keep a close eye on key market developments following the latest Fed decision. "The Fed held its policy rate steady overnight, as expected. However, external risks persist due to lingering tensions in the Middle East, concerns over the fiscal soundness of major countries and uncertainties surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) investment," BOK Senior Deputy Gov. Kwon Min-soo said in a separate statement. Kwon added that the central bank will closely monitor developments in financial and foreign exchange markets, with the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan also set to make rate decisions this week
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title_zh: 韩国将密切关注美国中期选举带来的影响
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body_zh: 韩国金融当局周四表示，将密切关注美国中期选举对金融市场的影响，如市场出现剧烈波动，将立即采取应对措施。美国联邦储备 overnight 维持基准利率不变后，韩国财政部长李亨il与韩国银行（BOK）行长申铉松、金融服务委员会主席李彦元以及金融监督院院长李宰镇就此事进行了讨论。美联储以10票赞成、2票反对的决定，将利率维持在3.75%-4.00%的区间。该决定使韩国与美国的关键利率差距最高达到1个百分点。李亨il说：“这一决定似乎反映出，美联储在评估9月加息及其他经济指标，以确定未来政策方向的同时，继续专注于稳定消费者价格。”李亨il指出，主要科技企业的盈利和投资前景，以及全球油价走势，正在加剧国内外金融市场的波动。财政部长补充道：“中期选举后，我们还需要关注美国国会的构成、政治格局变化背景下华盛顿对外政策的调整及其对市场的影响。”不过，李亨il表示，韩国经济基本面依然稳健，第三季度国内生产总值（GDP）环比增长1%。财政部长指出，美国选举和法国财政不稳定也可能对政府债券市场产生不利影响，并表示韩国将在必要时与相关机构合作，及时采取市场稳定措施，例如紧急回购债券。李亨il还表示，他将与相关参与方讨论如何将目前T+2的股票结算周期缩短至T+1。李亨il说：“缩短结算周期是一项重要任务，因为它能够降低相关风险并提高资金管理效率。”他指出，政府将就此事征询市场参与者的意见。与此同时，韩国银行表示，将继续密切关注美联储最新决定后的重要市场动态。韩国银行高级副行长权民秀在一份单独声明中说：“美联储如预期般 overnight 维持政策利率不变。然而，中东紧张局势持续、主要国家财政稳健性受到质疑，以及人工智能（AI）投资前景的不确定性，使外部风险依然存在。”权民秀补充称，韩国央行将密切关注金融和外汇市场的发展；欧洲中央银行和日本银行也将于本周作出利率决定

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/pol.body: The government plans to designate six new public housing zones in Gyeonggi Province, surrounding Seoul, to build more than 76,700 homes as part of efforts to boost the housing supply, the land ministry said Thursday. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport announced the six candidate sites as a follow-up to its August plan to supply 100,000 new homes. The proposed sites are located in Gimpo, Guri, Hanam, Uijeongbu and Goyang in Gyeonggi Province, all within 5 kilometers of Seoul's boundaries and offering relatively easy access to the capital. The ministry said the sites are located in greenbelt areas where environmental conservation value has already been diminished, making them suitable for systematic development. Land Minister Hong Jee-sun stressed the need to expand the housing supply in areas favored by young people and newlyweds, pledging government support to accelerate construction

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title: S. Korea, US, partners reaffirm N. Korea denuclearization goal, back sanctions enforcement
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary: WASHINGTON — South Korea, the United States and other like-minded partners on Wednesday reaffirmed their commitment to the denuclearization of North Korea, highlighting recent sanctions targeting Pyongyang's overseas workers, cyber activities and military cooperation with Russia.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.summary_zh: 华盛顿——韩国、美国及其他志同道合的伙伴周三再次承诺推动朝鲜无核化，并强调近期针对平壤海外劳工、网络活动以及与俄罗斯军事合作的制裁。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: WASHINGTON — South Korea, the United States and other like-minded partners on Wednesday reaffirmed their commitment to the denuclearization of North Korea, highlighting recent sanctions targeting Pyongyang's overseas workers, cyber activities and military cooperation with Russia. In a joint statement issued by 11 countries and the European Union, the participants welcomed sanctions imposed by the U.S., Australia and the European Union in October to disrupt North Korea's efforts to finance its nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs. The statement was issued by South Korea, the U.S., Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Britain and the EU. The countries highlighted findings by the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT), which shed light on Pyongyang's military cooperation with Russia, cyber-enabled IT worker schemes and overseas labor operations. The team was established after a U.N. expert panel, tasked with monitoring sanctions enforcement, was disbanded in April 2024 due to Russia's veto of a resolution to extend its mandate. It consists of 11 countries, including South Korea, the United States, Japan, Australia and Canada. "The MSMT and EU reaffirm our commitment to the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the DPRK," the statement said, referring to the North's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The participants also urged all United Nations member states, particularly permanent members of the Security Council, to fully implement sanctions resolutions against North Korea. Earlier in the day, the U.S. Treasury Department announced fresh sanctions against 10 individuals and one entity accused of facilitating North Korean IT worker schemes targeting American businesses and generating illicit revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.title_zh: 韩国、美国及合作伙伴重申朝鲜无核化目标，支持加强制裁执行
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 华盛顿——韩国、美国及其他志同道合的伙伴于星期三重申了推动朝鲜无核化的承诺，并强调近期针对平壤海外劳工、网络活动以及与俄罗斯军事合作的制裁。在11个国家和欧盟发表的一份联合声明中，参与方对美国、澳大利亚和欧盟于10月实施的制裁表示欢迎，这些制裁旨在阻碍朝鲜为核武器和弹道导弹计划筹资的努力。声明由韩国、美国、澳大利亚、加拿大、法国、德国、意大利、日本、荷兰、新西兰、英国和欧盟发布。这些国家强调了多边制裁监测小组（MSMT）的调查结果，该小组揭示了平壤与俄罗斯的军事合作、利用网络手段运作的信息技术劳工计划以及海外劳工行动。该小组是在一个负责监督制裁执行的联合国专家小组于2024年4月因俄罗斯否决延长其授权的决议而被解散后成立的。小组成员包括11个国家，其中有韩国、美国、日本、澳大利亚和加拿大。声明称：“MSMT和欧盟重申我们致力于实现朝鲜民主主义人民共和国完全、可核查且不可逆的无核化。”声明中“朝鲜”指的是朝鲜的正式名称朝鲜民主主义人民共和国。参与方还敦促联合国所有会员国，特别是安全理事会常任理事国，全面执行针对朝鲜的制裁决议。当天早些时候，美国财政部宣布对10名个人和1个实体实施新制裁，这些个人和实体被指控协助朝鲜利用信息技术劳工计划针对美国企业，并为平壤的武器计划创造非法收入

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: SEATTLE — A former U.S. diplomat said it is "very unusual" for Korean lawmakers to have their official visits disrupted by visa complications, suggesting that stricter interpretations of U.S. immigration rules may be behind the recent difficulties. His comments came after Rep. Jin Sung-joon, chair of the National Assembly's defense committee, disclosed that his U.S. visa application had been marked "refused" ahead of a planned visit to Hawaii in early November.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 西雅图——一名前美国外交官表示，韩国议员因签证问题而无法按计划进行正式访问“非常不同寻常”，并暗示，近期遇到的困难可能源于美国移民规则得到更严格的解释。此前，国会国防委员会主席 Jin Sung-joon 披露，他的美国签证申请已被标注为“拒签”，而他原计划于11月初前往夏威夷访问。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: SEATTLE — A former U.S. diplomat said it is "very unusual" for Korean lawmakers to have their official visits disrupted by visa complications, suggesting that stricter interpretations of U.S. immigration rules may be behind the recent difficulties. Henry Haggard, a former minister counselor for political affairs at the U.S. Embassy in Seoul who now heads a Washington, D.C.-based geopolitical advisory firm, said additional screening for applicants with criminal records is normal, but such procedures have historically rarely prevented senior officials from traveling to the United States on official business. His comments came after Rep. Jin Sung-joon, chair of the National Assembly's defense committee, disclosed that his U.S. visa application had been marked "refused" ahead of a planned visit to Hawaii in early November. Jin was scheduled to lead a parliamentary delegation for meetings with senior U.S. military officials, including Adm. Samuel Paparo, commander of U.S. Indo-Pacific Command. The incident followed a visa delay involving Rep. Jung Chung-rae earlier this month, which forced him to change his planned overseas parliamentary audit itinerary. Haggard said the U.S. Embassy historically worked closely with the State Department and Department of Homeland Security in Washington to facilitate official visits, while keeping South Korean officials informed of possible delays. Such coordination generally allowed trips to proceed, sometimes after minor delays, he said. "Rather than diplomatic shifts, these are most likely due to a stricter interpretation of the rules that limit or prohibit travel by those who have criminal records," Haggard said. He suggested similar difficulties could be occurring elsewhere. Haggard also warned that the visa complications could damage bilateral relations, noting that many South Koreans regard the anti-government protests of the 1980s as central to the country's democratization. He said the violent and anti-American nature of some protests could make U.S. visa waivers harder to obtain, while potentially prompting even strongly pro-American Koreans to reconsider their favorable views of the United States. Jin reportedly was asked to submit court records related to a 1991 conviction under South Korea's National Security Act. He was pardoned in 1995. The State Department's visa tracking system listed his application as "Refused" as of Oct. 28, although that status can also apply to cases undergoing administrative processing. South Korea's foreign ministry has indicated that the application process may still be ongoing
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 美国前外交官：韩国议员遭遇美国签证问题“非常不同寻常”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 西雅图——一名美国前外交官表示，韩国议员因签证问题导致正式访问行程受阻“非常不寻常”，并暗示，近期困难可能源于美国对移民法规作出了更严格的解释。曾任美国驻首尔大使馆政治事务公使、现领导一家总部位于华盛顿特区的地缘政治咨询公司的亨利·哈加德说，对有犯罪记录的申请人进行额外审查属于正常程序，但此类程序过去很少阻止高级官员赴美执行公务。他的这番评论是在韩国国会国防委员会主席金星埙披露其美国签证申请在计划于11月初访问夏威夷前被标注为“拒签”之后发表的。金星埙原计划率领一个议员代表团，与包括美国印太司令部司令塞缪尔·帕帕罗海军上将在内的美国高级军事官员会面。此前，本月早些时候，韩国议员郑清莱也因签证延误而被迫调整原定的海外议会审计行程。哈加德说，美国大使馆过去通常会与华盛顿的美国国务院和国土安全部密切协作，为正式访问提供便利，同时让韩国官员了解可能出现的延误。他说，这种协调一般能够确保行程成行，有时只会稍有延误。“这更可能是因为对限制或禁止有犯罪记录者出境的规则作出了更严格的解释，而不是外交政策发生了变化。”哈加德说。他暗示，其他地方可能也出现了类似困难。哈加德还警告称，签证问题可能损害韩美双边关系，并指出，许多韩国人将20世纪80年代的反对政府抗议视为韩国民主化的重要组成部分。他说，部分抗议具有暴力性和反美性质，可能使韩国人更难获得美国免签待遇，也可能促使即使强烈亲美的韩国人重新审视他们对美国的友好看法。据报道，金星埙被要求提交与韩国《国家安全法》下1991年定罪有关的法院记录。他于1995年获得赦免。截至10月28日，美国国务院的签证追踪系统将其申请列为“拒签”，不过这一状态也可能适用于仍在接受行政处理的案件。韩国外交部表示，申请程序可能仍在进行中……

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title: US sanctions N. Korean network accused of defrauding businesses
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on Wednesday to target what the Treasury Department said were North Korean government-run schemes that use IT workers to defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs. The Treasury Department said the schemes involve North Korean IT workers fraudulently gaining employment with companies in the United States and elsewhere, and Pyongyang taking most of the workers' wages to fund its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.summary_zh: 美国于周三实施制裁，以打击美国财政部所称由朝鲜政府掌控、利用信息技术人员诈骗美国企业并为平壤武器计划创造收入的阴谋。财政部称，这些阴谋涉及朝鲜信息技术人员通过欺诈手段在 美国及其他地区的公司获得就业，随后平壤拿走这些人员的大部分工资，为其大规模杀伤性武器和弹道导弹计划提供资金。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: The United States imposed sanctions on Wednesday to target what the Treasury Department said were North Korean government-run schemes that use IT workers to defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs. The Treasury Department said the schemes involve North Korean IT workers fraudulently gaining employment with companies in the United States and elsewhere, and Pyongyang taking most of the workers' wages to fund its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. "These networks permeate through the global financial system, necessitating a unified response to match the threat," the department said in a statement, adding that Australia and the European Union also imposed North Korea-related sanctions this month. North Korea's mission to the United Nations in New York did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The sanctions come as U.S. President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but Pyongyang has shown little interest in diplomacy aimed at containing its nuclear program. However, earlier this month Trump downplayed the idea of another high-profile meeting with Kim in China next month. Trump became the only U.S. president to have met a North Korean leader when he held an unprecedented series of summits with Kim in 2018 and 2019, but the diplomatic efforts broke down over U.S. demands that North Korea give up its nuclear weapons. Trump has since referred to North Korea repeatedly as a "nuclear power," although his administration has continued to call for the country's denuclearization and has not formally recognized it as a nuclear-weapons state. The Treasury Department sanctioned a separate North Korean IT worker network in March
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 美国制裁被控诈骗企业的朝鲜网络
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 美国于周三实施制裁，以打击美国财政部所称的朝鲜政府运作的欺诈计划。这些计划利用信息技术 workers 欺诈美国企业，并为平壤的武器计划创造收入。财政部表示，这些计划涉及朝鲜信息技术人员以欺诈手段受雇于美国及其他地区的公司，而平壤则拿走这些人员的大部分工资，为其大规模杀伤性武器和弹道导弹计划提供资金。该部门在一份声明中表示：“这些网络渗透全球金融体系，因此需要采取统一行动，以应对相关威胁。”声明还指出，澳大利亚和欧盟本月也实施了与朝鲜有关的制裁。朝鲜常驻联合国代表团在纽约没有立即回应置评请求。此项制裁出台之际，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普一直急于重启与朝鲜的谈判，但平壤对旨在遏制其核计划的外交谈判兴趣不大。不过，特朗普本月早些时候淡化了下月在中国再次与金正恩举行高调会晤的想法。2018年和2019年，特朗普与金正恩举行了一系列前所未有的峰会，成为首位与朝鲜领导人会面的美国总统，但美国要求朝鲜放弃核武器，外交努力因此破裂。此后，特朗普多次将朝鲜称为“核国家”，尽管其政府仍继续呼吁朝鲜实现无核化，并且尚未正式承认朝鲜为核武器国家。财政部3月还制裁了一个独立的朝鲜信息技术人员网络

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/20.body: Korea will ease export restrictions currently imposed on diesel starting in November on condition that domestic supply remains stable, the industry ministry said Thursday. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said the government will allow diesel exports of up to 110 percent of the volume recorded in the same month a year earlier, up from the current cap of 100 percent. The higher cap will apply only when oil refiners fulfill their domestic supply obligations and maintain adequate inventories, the ministry added. Korea adopted export restrictions on fuel products when it implemented the oil price cap system in March to maintain stable domestic supply. Local oil refiners have recently called for such restrictions to be eased. The industry ministry said crude supplies remain stable, citing crude import volumes for October and November equivalent to at least 100 percent of last year's monthly average. "With tensions in the Middle East lingering, the government will closely monitor the supply of petroleum products and immediately reinstate the previous cap should further supply concerns arise," a ministry official said

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.body: The federal government yesterday defended its proposed $21.7 billion external borrowing plan, insisting that the funds would finance productive investments in infrastructure and other critical sectors to stimulate economic growth, strengthen national productivity and improve living standards. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the proposed financing should be assessed based on the assets to be created and the economic returns expected, rather than simply as an addition to the country’s debt burden. Oyedele spoke after the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the State House, Abuja, amid criticism of the borrowing plan by former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, as well as the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Peter Obi. Oyedele maintained that the proposal was a financing plan and did not mean the federal government had already borrowed the money or would necessarily draw down the entire amount. “Altogether, if you convert the euro amount and add it to the dollar amount, it will come up to $21.7 billion. First and foremost, this is a plan. It doesn’t mean that we have borrowed. It doesn’t even mean that we borrow all of it. So it’s a plan. The average lifespan of the projects under this plan is five years. This qualifies as investment. This is investment, not borrowing,” Oyedele pointed out. The proposed financing comprises $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion for projects and programmes covering transportation, security, healthcare, agriculture, energy, digital infrastructure, education and social protection. The government said transportation infrastructure accounts for approximately $10.6 billion, including major projects such as the Sokoto-Badagry and Lagos-Calabar highways and the Kano-Kaduna rail project. Oyedele said the government was pursuing financing from multilateral and bilateral development partners, alongside other sources, to implement the projects. Besides, about $7.9 billion is expected from multilateral and bilateral partners, with the World Bank among the major institutions providing support. Oyedele said a $5 billion World Bank component would attract concessional financing at an average interest rate of about 2.1 per cent, while some social-sector loans would carry interest rates of around 2 per cent. He said the government was prioritising favourable financing terms to reduce borrowing costs and ensure that the projects delivered lasting economic benefits. The minister also disclosed that the federal government was targeting single-digit inflation by the end of 2027, as it intensifies efforts to stabilise prices and sustain economic growth. He said inflation had declined to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year, after peaking at about 34 per cent. According to him, FEC resolved to intensify efforts to bring down prices, particularly food prices, while sustaining investments in infrastructure, human capital development and job creation. Oyedele disclosed that Nigeria’s foreign reserves had risen above $55 billion, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves had increased to more than $45 billion from less than $1 billion three years ago. He put economic growth at 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, compared with 2.74 per cent in May 2023. The minister added that the tax-to-GDP ratio had risen from about seven per cent in 2023 to 12.5 per cent by the end of 2025, while the debt-service-to-revenue ratio had declined from 97 per cent to below 60 per cent. Oyedele also defended the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the previous arrangement placed an unsustainable burden on public finances and constrained the government’s ability to invest in infrastructure and essential services. He said Nigeria had increased petrol prices about 3,050 times in 50 years without resolving the underlying subsidy problem, adding that the government had introduced interventions to cushion the impact of economic reforms on vulnerable Nigerians. According to him, more than 10 million households had received over N600 billion in cash transfers, while the Nigerian Education Loan Fund had disbursed N372.6 billion to more than 1.5 million students. He added that more than 800,000 micro, small and medium-sized enterprises had benefited from subsidised loans at single-digit interest rates. The minister further said low-income earners making up to N100,000 monthly were exempt from personal income tax, while businesses with annual turnover of up to N100 million were exempt from corporate income tax, value-added tax and withholding tax under the relevant tax reforms. He also disclosed that the Nigerian capital market had grown from about N30 trillion to more than N160 trillion, expressing optimism about the naira’s outlook on the strength of improved foreign reserves and other economic fundamentals. The federal government also said it was working towards presenting the 2027 budget before the end of the year to allow the National Assembly sufficient time to consider the proposed fiscal framework ahead of the next financial year. The Minister of State for Budget, Doris Uzoka-Anite, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the FEC meeting. “We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” she said. Further details of the proposed budget, including its overall size, revenue projections, deficit estimates and allocations to key sectors, are expected to emerge as preparations progress. Similarly, the federal government has approved the commencement of procurement for the proposed East and West Super Grids as part of efforts to expand electricity transmission capacity from about 5,000 megawatts to 19,000MW within two years. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who disclosed this after the FEC meeting, said the projects would strengthen the national grid and enable more electricity to be transmitted to consumers. He said the government had also approved three major interventions to reinforce transmission infrastructure around Abuja and Lagos, while accelerating efforts to clear more than 300 containers of electricity equipment stranded at the nation’s ports. The first approval covers the construction of a 33kV double-circuit underground and overhead line linked to the Katampe Transmission Substation, which serves the North-Central region. The second involves the design, manufacture and supply of three 300MVA, 330/132/33kV power transformers for the Ikeja West Transmission Substation, a critical facility supplying the Lagos axis. The third project entails the reconstruction and upgrade of the 35.6-kilometre Itumola-Mapasin-Shagamu 132kV single-circuit transmission line to a double-circuit line to accommodate rising electricity demand along the Lagos-Shagamu corridor. Tegbe said the projects formed part of the government’s broader strategy to improve transmission infrastructure, stabilise electricity supply and maximise the use of existing power-sector assets. He disclosed that the ministry had commenced a nationwide technical audit of electricity infrastructure, dividing the country into three major energy zones: Lagos and its surrounding industrial corridor; the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano axis; and the Enugu-Onitsha-Benin axis. According to him, the audit, which began four weeks ago, would identify ageing and weak infrastructure requiring replacement or rehabilitation to improve the reliability of the national grid. The minister also restated that the government had paid N1.23 trillion out of the N3.3 trillion owed to gas suppliers and other stakeholders, adding that the outstanding liabilities had contributed to difficulties in ensuring adequate gas supply to power generation companies. He said the government was working to improve the operational efficiency of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) and the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) particularly in coordinating grid management and infrastructure development. Tegbe explained that separating system operations from transmission infrastructure management was intended to improve efficiency, response times and coordination across the electricity network. He added that the government was reviewing options for greater private-sector participation in electricity asset management to improve performance and ensure better utilisation of existing infrastructure. On the super grids, Tegbe said the projects would strengthen transmission links across the northern and southern parts of the country, connecting Sokoto through Abuja and other locations to parts of the South. He said Tinubu had approved the commencement of the procurement process, describing the initiative as a significant step towards building a more resilient electricity network capable of supporting future demand. Tegbe also announced that construction had commenced on a new National Control Centre (NCC) in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which he said was built 64 years ago. The new centre is expected to strengthen the monitoring and management of the national grid. He further disclosed that the government was energising completed transmission substations in Kano, Katsina, Bauchi and Gombe, among other locations, to bring idle infrastructure into service. The minister said the government was also expanding access to electricity through solar mini-grids, particularly in institutions and locations facing transmission constraints. According to him, at least 14 federal universities had received installed and energised solar mini-grids, with capacities ranging from one megawatt to five megawatts. Another 11 universities were being supported through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund, bringing the number of institutions covered by the programme to nearly 30. He stated that five teaching hospitals were also benefiting from solar power installations being implemented in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health. On the backlog of electricity equipment stranded at the ports, Tegbe described the situation as unacceptable, saying some containers had reportedly remained uncleared for between 14 and 20 years. He said the president had directed the ministry to work with the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) and the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) to clear more than 300 containers containing electricity equipment. Tegbe attributed the prolonged delay to the failure of previous administrations to settle outstanding charges and complete the necessary clearance processes. In the same vein, FEC has approved N45.8 billion for a biosecurity and disease surveillance system at five international airports to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to detect Ebola and other dangerous pathogens at its borders. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate, disclosed this after the meeting, saying the project would be implemented under a 20-year public-private partnership concession awarded to BioHealth Consortium following the council’s approval of its full business case. Pate described the initiative as a major investment in Nigeria’s health and economic security, warning that infectious disease outbreaks could disrupt economic activities and threaten public safety. “Over the last two weeks, I think you realise the significance of enhancing biosecurity at our points of entry. Since COVID, we have known that there are significant vulnerabilities in terms of public health threats crossing borders and the need for coordinated, technology-driven systems for early warning, detection and response to emerging infectious disease threats,” he stressed. The surveillance system will be deployed at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos; Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja; Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano; Port Harcourt International Airport; and Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.title_zh: 联邦政府为217亿美元贷款辩护，称资金将用于生产性项目
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/f.body_zh: 联邦政府昨日为其拟议的217亿美元外债融资方案辩护，坚持表示，这笔资金将用于基础设施及其他关键部门的生产性投资，以刺激经济增长、增强国家生产力并改善生活水平。财政部长兼经济协调部长Taiwo Oyedele表示，评估拟议融资方案时，应依据将要创造的资产和预期经济回报，而不应仅将其视为国家债务负担的增加。Oyedele是在总统Bola Tinubu于阿布贾国家宫主持的联邦执行委员会（FEC）会议后发表上述言论的。当时，前副总统Atiku Abubakar，以及参加2027年选举的尼日利亚民主党（NDC）总统候选人Peter Obi均对该融资方案提出批评。Oyedele坚称，该提案是一项融资计划，并不意味着联邦政府已经借入了这笔资金，也不意味着政府必然会提取全部金额。他说：“总体而言，如果把欧元金额折算后加到美元金额上，总额将达到217亿美元。首先，这是一项计划。这不意味着我们已经借了钱，甚至不意味着我们会借入全部资金。因此，这是一项计划。该计划下项目的平均实施周期为五年。这符合投资性质。这是投资，不是借款。”Oyedele指出，拟议融资包括205.2亿美元和10.45亿欧元，用于交通、安全、医疗卫生、农业、能源、数字基础设施、教育和社会保护领域的项目与计划。政府表示，交通基础设施约占106亿美元，包括Sokoto-Badagry和Lagos-Calabar高速公路以及Kano-Kaduna铁路项目等重大工程。Oyedele说，政府正寻求多边和双边发展伙伴及其他来源的融资，以实施这些项目。此外，预计约79亿美元将来自多边和双边伙伴，世界银行是提供支持的主要机构之一。Oyedele表示，世界银行提供的50亿美元部分将获得优惠融资，平均利率约为2.1%，部分社会领域贷款的利率约为2%。他说，政府正优先争取有利的融资条件，以降低借贷成本，并确保项目带来持久的经济效益。部长还透露，随着政府加大力度稳定物价并维持经济增长，联邦政府的目标是在2027年底前将通胀率降至个位数。他说，通胀率已从此前一度达到约34%的峰值降至9月的14.63%，而上年同期为20.98%。据他介绍，FEC决定加大力度压低物价，尤其是食品价格，同时维持对基础设施、人力资源开发和就业创造的投入。Oyedele透露，尼日利亚外汇储备已升至550亿美元以上，达到18年来最高水平；净储备也由三年前不足10亿美元增至逾450亿美元。他表示，第二季度经济增长率为4.43%，相比之下，2023年5月为2.74%。部长补充称，税收占国内生产总值的比率已从2023年的约7%升至2025年底的12.5%，而偿债占收入比率则从97%降至60%以下。Oyedele还为取消汽油补贴辩护，认为此前的安排给公共财政造成不可持续的重负，并限制政府投资基础设施和基本服务的能力。他说，尼日利亚在50年间约3,050次上调汽油价格，却未能解决潜在的补贴问题；政府还推出干预措施，以缓冲经济改革对脆弱的尼日利亚人造成的影响。据他介绍，超过1,000万户家庭已获得逾6,000亿奈拉现金转移支付，尼日利亚教育贷款基金也已向逾150万名学生发放3,726亿奈拉。他补充说，超过80万家微型企业、小型和中型企业获得了低个位数利率的补贴贷款。部长进一步表示，根据相关税收改革改革，月收入不超过10万奈拉的低收入者免征个人所得税，年营业额不超过1亿奈拉的企业免征企业所得税、增值税和预提税。他还透露，尼日利亚资本市场已从约30万亿奈拉增至逾160万亿奈拉，并对奈拉前景表示乐观，理由是外汇储备及其他经济基本面有所改善。联邦政府还表示，正努力在年底前提交2027年度预算，以便为国民议会留出充足时间，在下一财政年度开始前审议拟议财政框架。预算国务部长Doris Uzoka-Anite在FEC会议后向记者介绍情况时说：“我们正在制定2027年度预算，计划在年底前提交。”随着准备工作推进，拟议预算的更多细节，包括总体规模、收入预测、赤字估算以及向重点领域的拨款，预计将陆续公布。同样，联邦政府已批准启动拟议东部和西部超级电网的采购工作，努力在两年内将输电能力从约5,000兆瓦提升至19,000MW。电力部长Joseph Tegbe在FEC会议后透露此事，并表示这些项目将强化国家电网，使更多电力能够输送给消费者。他说，政府还批准了加强阿布贾和拉各斯周边输电基础设施的三项重大干预措施，同时加快清理滞留在全国各港口的300多个电力设备集装箱。第一项批准涉及建设一条与Katampe输电变电站相连的33kV双回路地下及架空线路，该变电站服务于中北部地区。第二项涉及为Ikeja West输电变电站设计、制造和供应三台300MVA、330/132/33kV电力变压器，该设施是向拉各斯轴线供电的关键设施。第三个项目包括将35.6公里的Itumola-Mapasin-Shagamu 132kV单回路输电线路重建并升级为双回路线路，以满足Lagos-Shagamu走廊不断增长的用电需求。Tegbe表示，这些项目是政府改善输电基础设施、稳定电力供应并最大限度利用现有电力行业资产整体战略的一部分。他透露，电力部已启动全国电力基础设施技术审计，将全国划分为三大能源区：拉各斯及其周边工业走廊；Abuja-Kaduna-Kano轴线；以及Enugu-Onitsha-Benin轴线。据他介绍，审计于四周前启动，将确定需要更换或修复的老化和薄弱基础设施，以提高国家电网可靠性。部长还重申，政府已从欠付天然气供应商及其他利益相关方的3.3万亿奈拉中支付了1.23万亿奈拉，并指出未偿债务导致难以确保向发电公司供应充足天然气。他说，政府正努力提高尼日利亚输电公司（TCN）和尼日利亚独立系统运营商（NISO）的运营效率，尤其是在电网管理和基础设施开发方面的协调能力。Tegbe解释，将系统运营与输电基础设施管理分开，旨在提高整个电力网络的效率、响应速度和协调水平。他补充说，政府正在研究扩大私营部门参与电力资产管理、提高绩效并确保现有基础设施得到更充分利用的方案。关于超级电网，Tegbe表示，这些项目将加强尼日利亚南北部之间的输电联系，把Sokoto经阿布贾及其他地点与南部部分地区连接起来。他说，Tinubu已批准启动采购程序，并将这项倡议描述为建设更具韧性的电力网络、使其能够支撑未来用电需求的重要一步。Tegbe还宣布，位于奥索博博的新国家控制中心（NCC）已经开工，将取代现有设施；据他说，现有设施建于64年前。新中心预计将加强国家电网的监控与管理。他还透露，政府正在为Kano、Katsina、Bauchi和Gombe等地的已完工输电变电站通电，使闲置基础设施投入运行。部长表示，政府还通过太阳能微电网扩大电力供应范围，特别是在面临输电限制的机构和地区。据他介绍，至少14所联邦大学已安装并接入太阳能微电网，容量从1兆瓦至5兆瓦不等。另有11所大学正通过高等教育信托基金获得支持，使该计划覆盖的机构总数增至近30所。他表示，五家教学医院也将受益于与联邦卫生部合作实施的太阳能发电设施。在滞留在港口的电力设备积压问题上，Tegbe称这一状况“不可接受”，并表示据报道一些集装箱已有14年至20年未获清关。他说，总统已指示该部与尼日利亚港务局（NPA）及尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）合作，清运300多个装有电力设备的集装箱。Tegbe将长期延误归咎于历届政府未能缴清未付费用并完成必要的清关程序。与此同时，FEC已批准为五个国际机场的生物安全和疾病监测系统拨款458亿奈拉，以加强尼日利亚在边境发现埃博拉及其他危险病原体的能力。卫生与社会福利协调部长Ali Pate教授在会后透露，该项目将根据一项为期20年的公私合作伙伴特许安排实施；内阁批准BioHealth Consortium的完整商业计划后，该特许权已授予该财团。Pate称，这项倡议是对尼日利亚卫生和经济安全的重大投资，并警告说，传染病暴发可能扰乱经济活动并威胁公众安全。他强调：“过去两周，我认为大家已经意识到加强入境口岸生物安全的重要性。自COVID以来，我们就知道，公共卫生威胁跨境传播方面存在重大脆弱性，也需要协调一致、由技术驱动的系统，对新出现的传染病威胁进行预警、检测和响应。”该监测系统将部署于拉各斯Murtala Muhammed国际机场、阿布贾Nnamdi Azikiwe国际机场、Kano的Mallam Aminu Kano国际机场、Port Harcourt国际机场以及Enugu的Akanu Ibiam国际机场。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.title: TUC Rejects FG’s N70,000 Transport Allowance, Demands Salary Increase
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.summary: Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) yesterday objected to the federal government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance to civil servants, saying temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The federal government had approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the effects of rising living costs.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.summary_zh: 尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）昨日反对联邦政府拟向公务员发放每月N70,000交通津贴，称临时性加薪奖励不可持续，也难以长期推行。联邦政府已批准自2026年11月起，为各级公共服务人员连续6个月每月发放N70,000交通津贴，以缓解生活成本上涨带来的影响。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.body: Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) yesterday objected to the federal government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance to civil servants, saying temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The objection came as former Vice President and presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, described the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate last-minute attempt to contain public anger. The federal government had approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, to cushion the effects of rising living costs. The approval was announced in a memorandum of understanding (MoU) issued at the end of a conciliation meeting between government representatives and leaders of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) in Abuja on Tuesday. The MoU was signed by Tanimu Yakubu, Director-General of the budget office; Joe Ajaero, NLC President; Garba Abdul, Permanent Secretary of the Service Welfare Office in the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation; and Muhammad Dingyadi, Minister of Labour and Employment. However, TUC demanded immediate salary increase for workers and implementation of agreement reached with Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU). TUC said its position was taken at its National Administrative Council meeting on October 8 in Abuja, where it sent a demand letter to the federal government through the office of Secretary to Government of the Federation. A statement signed by TUC President, Festus Osifo, said the union would await the outcome of a meeting with the federal government to decide on the next steps to take. The congress said the letter was in furtherance of an earlier press briefing on the economic hardship facing workers and proposed measures to address it. On salary increase, TUC said its position was clear that the federal government should review and increase the salaries of workers. It said the government did not require any minimum wage negotiation before increasing pay, as there was no maximum wage law in the country. It stated that some states had raised minimum wage above N100,000, adding that the federal government could raise the pay of its lowest workers to N300,000, from the current N70,000, and apply consequential adjustment. “While it is good to negotiate minimum wage, which will affect other cadre of workers, FGN must raise wage level immediately as there are no law or historical practices stopping it from doing so,” TUC stated. Following the letter, the TUC leadership held consultative meetings with government officials, including Secretary to Government of Federation, where its position was canvassed. It said the proposal of wage award was mentioned, but it was vehemently rejected for several reasons. According to TUC, temporary wage awards are not sustainable and far-reaching. The congress cited the wage award agreed on October 2, 2023, which was to be implemented until the minimum wage was agreed in 2024, but was never implemented holistically, with some workers still owed one or two months while others never received it. TUC stated, “How do we go back to same wage award that never benefited all workers? How can workers be expected to trust fresh promises when previous obligations remain outstanding?” It also cited irregularity in the payment of the 2023 wage award, where those who got up to four months of N40,000 never got it monthly but at intervals, while over 80 per cent of states and the informal sector never implemented any wage award. “From the foregoing, we further reiterate our demand for pay raise for all government workers, as salary is only consistent and far-reaching pay that workers could rely upon,” TUC said. It stressed that negotiations of a new national minimum wage must not become an excuse for postponing urgent pay increment. On cost-of-living relief, TUC said economic crisis affected not only federal workers but also state and local government workers, as well as pensioners, private sector and informal economy workers. It called on government at all levels to implement measurable interventions to reduce the cost of essential goods, ensure timely payment of salaries and pensions, and revitalise the productive sector. On JOHESU, Osifo said he led the organised labour team that included the JOHESU leadership to resolve the industrial action that lasted several months. He said after several meetings at the Federal Ministry of Health, a final conciliatory meeting was held at Ministry of Labour and Employment, where a communique was agreed. The signing led to suspension of the industrial action in good faith, but TUC said the government did not keep its side. Under the terms of settlement, it was agreed that all outstanding issues relating to CONHESS adjustment shall be conclusively addressed without further delay, but seven months later, adjustment remained unimplemented, Osifo said. “This continued failure to honour explicit commitment violates principle of good faith, undermines confidence in collective bargaining, and is absolutely unacceptable,” the TUC said. It demanded immediate implementation of CONHESS adjustment, clear timetable, budgetary provisions, and resolution of outstanding matters. TUC said its position was unequivocal that workers were demanding social and economic justice, adding that it would defend workers’ rights without retreat and pursue every legitimate avenue to compel government to honour obligations. It said it awaited the final outcome of scheduled meetings with the government to decide the next line of action. Meanwhile, Atiku condemned the N70,000 monthly transport support for public service workers as a desperate attempt by the federal government to contain public anger. He said it was an admittance that government policies had made life unbearable for millions of citizens. In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said, “The Tinubu administration is scrambling from one announcement to another, showing its failure to grasp the crisis. The cost-of-living crisis reaches beyond transport: energy, food, rent and other essentials affect every part of daily life. “Barbers pay more to power their clippers; restaurant owners face higher cooking costs; shopkeepers struggle to keep prices down; school bus operators pay more for fuel; and families still must buy food. Every business and household are affected. Does hardship end at the bus stop?” The statement said, “If public service workers receive N70,000 monthly for transport from November, what happens to private sector workers, traders, small businesses, transport operators and millions without formal jobs? The public workforce is only a fraction of Nigeria’s population. A temporary allowance for some cannot solve a national crisis. “The agreement also leaves the effective date for a new minimum wage unresolved. The government must publish payment dates, explain eligibility and say when wage negotiations will produce a decision.” Atiku said, “Any genuine relief is welcome, but a six-month allowance cannot undo this hardship. At about N1,400 per litre, N70,000 buys roughly 50 litres of petrol. What meaningful difference can 50 litres make over an entire month? “What Nigerians are witnessing is a government that set the house ablaze with its reckless policies, then pretends to fight the inferno by throwing ice cubes at the flames. A temporary N70,000 allowance cannot extinguish a cost-of-living crisis this government ignited. “This is the pattern: the fuel discount failed, the 90-day cost of living plan failed before it began, and now comes another temporary payment. The government promised CNG would lower transport costs, but that promise has failed. For Nigerians still paying more to commute, the CNG programme is another scam of promises, while families face the same unaffordable prices.” The statement added, “These rushed announcements smack of political bribery and corruption. Tinubu has shown no genuine intention of clearing the monumental mess caused by his hasty subsidy removal. He offers temporary payments instead of confronting the consequences. “Atiku has proposed a practical alternative: a transparently managed production subsidy for fuel refined in Nigeria, delivering relief at the pump. Tinubu must not punish 250 million Nigerians for the corruption and leakages of a few thousand. His arrogance prevents him from reconsidering a cocky decision, while families and businesses pay the price. “N70,000 may help with transport, but it cannot explain why work, food and running a business have become unaffordable. Nigerians need lasting relief, decent wages and an economy that rewards honest work. When will life become affordable again?” Atiku said his campaign would pursue practical measures to lower living costs, raise household incomes, and restore dignity to work. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.title_zh: 工会大会拒绝联邦政府发放的70,000奈拉交通津贴，要求提高工资
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/t.body_zh: 尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）昨天反对联邦政府拟向公务员发放N70,000交通津贴，称临时性加薪措施既不可持续，也无法带来广泛持久的效果。反对之际，非洲民主大会（ADC）前副总统兼总统候选人阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔将每月向公共服务人员提供的N70,000交通补贴描述为联邦政府为平息公众愤怒而作出的绝望的最后努力。联邦政府已批准自2026年11月起，连续六个月向各级公共服务人员每月发放N70,000交通津贴，以缓解生活成本上涨的影响。该批准是在政府代表与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）领导人周二于阿布贾举行的调解会议结束时签署的一份谅解备忘录（MoU）中公布的。谅解备忘录由预算办公室主任塔尼穆·亚库布、NLC主席乔·阿贾埃罗、联邦公务员首长办公室公务员福利办公室常任秘书加尔巴·阿卜杜勒，以及劳工与就业部长穆罕马德·丁亚迪签署。然而，TUC要求立即为工人加薪，并落实与联合卫生部门工会（JOHESU）达成的协议。TUC表示，其立场是在10月8日于阿布贾举行的全国行政委员会会议上确定的，并在会上通过联邦政府秘书办公室向联邦政府递交了一份要求信。TUC主席费斯图斯·奥西福签署的声明称，该工会将等待与联邦政府会议的结果，再决定下一步行动。工会大会表示，这封信是对此前有关工人面临经济困境及拟议应对措施的新闻简报的进一步跟进。关于加薪，TUC表示其立场十分明确，即联邦政府应重新审查并提高工人薪酬。TUC称，政府在提高薪酬前无须进行任何最低工资谈判，因为该国没有最高工资法。TUC指出，一些州已将最低工资提高至N100,000以上，并补充说，联邦政府可以把最低级别工人的薪酬从目前的N70,000提高到N300,000，同时实行连带调整。TUC称：“协商最低工资固然重要，因为这将影响其他类别的工作人员，但联邦政府必须立即提高工资水平，因为没有任何法律或历史惯例阻止其这样做。”递交信件后，TUC领导层与包括联邦政府秘书在内的政府官员举行磋商会议，向他们阐明自身立场。TUC表示，会上提到了加薪方案，但该方案因若干理由遭到强烈反对。据TUC称，临时加薪措施既不可持续，也难以产生广泛持久的效果。工会大会援引了2023年10月2日商定的加薪方案，该方案原定实施至2024年确定最低工资之日，但从未得到全面落实；一些工人仍被拖欠一至两个月工资，另一些人则从未领到这笔工资。TUC称：“我们怎能再次回到那个从未让所有工人受益的加薪方案？在先前的义务仍未履行的情况下，我们怎能指望工人相信新的承诺？”TUC还指出，2023年加薪方案在发放过程中存在不规律现象；有些工人最多可领取四个月、每月N40,000的加薪，但款项并非按月发放，而是间隔发放；超过80%的州和非正规部门则从未落实任何加薪方案。TUC表示：“鉴于上述情况，我们再次重申要求提高所有政府工作人员薪酬，因为薪酬是唯一稳定持久、能够信赖的报酬。”TUC强调，协商新的全国最低工资绝不能成为推迟紧急加薪的借口。在缓解生活成本压力方面，TUC表示，经济危机不仅影响联邦政府工作人员，也影响州和地方政府工作人员、退休金领取者、私营部门及非正规经济从业者。TUC呼吁各级政府采取可衡量的干预措施，降低 essentials等基本商品的成本，确保按时支付工资和退休金，并振兴生产部门。关于JOHESU，奥西福表示，他曾率领包括JOHESU领导层在内的劳工团队，解决了持续数月的行业行动。他说，在联邦卫生部举行多次会议后，劳工与就业部又举行了最后一次调解会议，各方就一份联合公报达成一致。签署公报促使行业行动出于善意而暂停，但TUC表示政府没有履行自己的义务。根据和解条款，所有与CONHESS调整有关的未决问题都应立即得到最终处理，但七个月后，该调整仍未落实。奥西福说：“这种持续不履行明确承诺的行为违反善意原则，削弱人们对集体谈判的信心，绝对不可接受。”TUC要求立即落实CONHESS调整、明确时间表、安排预算资金，并解决所有遗留问题。TUC表示，其立场毫不含糊，即工人正在争取社会和经济正义，并将坚定不移地捍卫工人权利，采取一切合法途径迫使政府履行义务。TUC称，将等待与政府既定会议的最后结果，再决定后续行动。与此同时，阿蒂库谴责每月向公共服务人员提供N70,000交通补贴，称这是联邦政府为平息公众愤怒而作出的绝望努力。他说，这等于承认政府政策已令数百万公民的生活难以忍受。ADC总统竞选委员会战略传播主任弗兰克·沙伊布发布声明称，阿蒂库表示：“蒂努布政府仓促地从一个公告转向另一个公告，表明其未能把握这场危机。生活成本危机不只涉及交通：能源、食物、房租及其他生活必需品影响着日常生活的每个方面。“理发师为电动理发器供电需要支付更多费用；餐馆老板面临更高的烹饪成本；店主努力维持较低售价；校车运营商支付更多燃油费；家庭依然需要购买食物。每一家企业和每一个家庭都受到影响。困难难道到公交站就结束了吗？”声明称：“如果公共服务人员从11月起每月获得N70,000交通补贴，私营部门工人、商贩、小企业、运输运营商以及数以百万计没有正式工作的人又该怎么办？公共部门工作人员只占尼日利亚人口的一小部分。向部分人员发放临时津贴，无法解决全国性危机。“该协议也没有确定新最低工资的生效日期。政府必须公布支付日期，说明资格条件，并说明工资协商何时能产生结果。”阿蒂库说：“任何真正有意义的纾困措施都值得欢迎，但六个月的津贴无法消除这些困难。在每升约N1,400的价格下，N70,000大约只能买50升汽油。整整一个月里，50升汽油能带来多大实际意义？“尼日利亚人目睹的是一个因鲁莽政策纵火烧掉自家、随后又假装通过向火焰扔冰块来扑灭大火的政府。每月N70,000的临时津贴无法熄灭本届政府亲手引发的这场生活成本危机。“这就是一贯的做法：燃油折扣失败了，90天生活成本计划尚未启动就已失败，现在又来了一笔临时付款。政府承诺压缩天然气将降低交通成本，但这一承诺已经落空。对仍在通勤中支付更高费用的尼日利亚人而言，压缩天然气计划不过是又一个骗局般的承诺，而家庭仍面对同样难以承受的价格。”声明补充道：“这些仓促发布的公告带有政治贿赂和腐败的味道。蒂努布没有表现出任何真正意图去处理其草率取消补贴所造成的严重烂摊子。他宁愿提供临时款项，也不愿面对取消补贴的后果。“阿蒂库提出了一项切实可行的替代方案：对在尼日利亚炼制的燃油实行透明管理的生产补贴，在加油站直接向消费者提供纾困。蒂努布不能因为少数人的腐败和流失，让2.5亿尼日利亚人受罚。他的傲慢使他无法重新考虑这个傲慢的决定，而家庭和企业却在为此买单。“N70,000或许有助于交通支出，但它无法解释为何工作、食物和经营企业都变得难以负担。尼日利亚人需要持久而有效的纾困、体面的工资，以及一个让诚实劳动获得回报的经济。生活在何时才能重新变得负担得起？”阿蒂库表示，他的竞选团队将推动切实措施，降低生活成本，提高家庭收入，并恢复劳动的尊严。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.title: Akpabio: 30 States Have Endorsed Constitution Amendment for State Police
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.summary: • Senate President expresses optimism over decentralised policing •Urges northern youths to mobilise support for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, on Wednesday disclosed that about 30 state Houses of Assembly had endorsed the proposed constitution amendment to establish state police.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.summary_zh: • 参议院议长对推行分散式警务表示乐观 • 敦促北部青年动员支持蒂努布在2027年再次参选 参议院议长戈德斯威尔·阿卡皮奥周三表示，已有约30个州议会赞同拟议的宪法修正案，以建立州级警察制度。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.body: • Senate President expresses optimism over decentralised policing •Urges northern youths to mobilise support for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, on Wednesday disclosed that about 30 state Houses of Assembly had endorsed the proposed constitution amendment to establish state police. Akpabio expressed optimism that Nigeria could soon adopt a decentralised policing system to strengthen national security. He spoke when members of Arewa Revival Project, a northern youth organisation with membership across the 19 northern states, visited him at his office in Abuja. The senate president said the proposed reform would improve the country’s capacity to tackle insecurity by bringing policing closer to communities. He expressed confidence that the constitution amendment process was nearing completion, adding that the establishment of state police would complement existing security structures and enhance efforts to address the country’s security challenges. He urged the youth to intensify grassroots mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, stating that continuity in government would allow the administration’s economic reforms and security policies to produce the desired results. Akpabio also called on the Nigerian youth to rise above what he described as paid social media propaganda against the administration. He said the president had taken significant steps to diversify the economy, reform the tax system, and address longstanding structural problems. The senate president expressed optimism that Nigeria would overcome its security challenges, urging the youth to remain confident in the country’s future while supporting efforts to restore peace and stability. He stated, “I always tell them that the devil that you see today, you will soon see them no more. Very soon, we shall overcome the insecurity that we face today. So, feel confident as you go round campaigning.” Akpabio maintained that decentralised policing would further strengthen national security, particularly by improving the ability of law enforcement agencies to respond to threats within their respective communities. He urged the Arewa youths to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying the administration needs time to consolidate its policies. He said the president had taken steps to move Nigeria away from its longstanding dependence on crude oil revenues and introduce reforms intended to reposition the economy. He said, “I expect the Nigerian youth to rise above social media propaganda because this president has managed to take us out of a mono-economy, an economy that was dependent only on crude oil. Akpabio stated that the administration’s performance had earned it the support of the National Assembly, declaring that lawmakers have endorsed Tinubu for a second term. He said, “No president has achieved the level of development that he has done in this country today since independence. The naysayers will not want to say so, but I am very proud and members of the National Assembly are very proud. Akpabio said Nigeria’s continued survival amid economic and security difficulties reflected the president’s willingness to confront the challenges facing the country. “I give glory to God that Nigeria is still surviving, and surviving because we have a president who thinks and somebody who wants to face challenges, and he is facing the challenges,” he said. He urged the youth to support continuity in government, stating that changing the administration before its policies fully matures could undermine the progress made so far. He stated, “You don’t change a winning team. He is doing so well. Allow his policies to crystallise. This is not somebody who is coming to experiment. He is already doing it.” Akpabio also emphasised the importance of youth participation in national development, saying government policies should create a stable foundation for future generations. He said, “Whatever we are doing today, we are doing it to stabilise your future and ensure the survival of Nigeria. So, it is good that you are seeing it.” He warned that the youth could face considerable challenges in countering criticism of the administration on social media, alleging that some individuals attacking the president and his supporters online are being paid to do so. Akpabio alleged, “It is not going to be easy for you because most of those who are attacking the president and attacking these young men on social media are being paid. You are not being paid.” He advised the youth to organise periodic grassroots engagements to explain government policies and challenge misinformation, rather than attempt to compete continuously with critics on social media. He said, “You may not be able to have the kind of energy and time with them. But once in a while, gather the youth together and let them see the truth and know the truth.” The visit provided an opportunity for the Arewa Revival Project to express support for Akpabio’s leadership of the National Assembly and recognise what it described as his contributions to national development. Earlier, Project Coordinator, Arewa Revival Project, Hon. Mustafa Ibrahim, said the organisation considered Akpabio deserving of recognition because of his contributions to nation-building and the achievements recorded under his leadership of the National Assembly. The group, whose membership spans the 19 northern states, presented the senate president with an award in recognition of his contributions to national development. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.title_zh: 阿卡比奥：已有30个州支持为州警察制度修改宪法
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/29/a.body_zh:
• 尼日利亚参议院议长对推行权力下放式警务表示乐观，敦促北部青年动员支持 Tinubu 2027年连任
参议院议长 Godswill Akpabio 周三透露，约有30个州议会赞成拟议的宪法修正案，以设立州警察。Akpabio 表示乐观，认为尼日利亚很快就能采用权力下放式警务制度，从而加强国家安全。当天，成员遍及北部19个州的青年组织 Arewa Revival Project 到办公室拜访他，会面地点位于阿布贾。

参议院议长表示，拟议中的改革将让警务更贴近社区，从而提升国家应对不安全局势的能力。他确信宪法修正程序即将完成，并补充说，设立州警察将补充现有安全架构，增强应对国家安全挑战的努力。

他敦促青年加强基层动员，支持总统 Bola Tinubu 在2027年再次参选，称政府延续执政将使本届政府的经济改革和安全政策取得预期成果。Akpabio 还呼吁尼日利亚青年超越他所说的针对本届政府的付费社交媒体宣传。他表示，总统已经采取重要举措，推动经济多元化、改革税收制度，并处理长期存在的结构性问题。

参议院议长乐观地表示，尼日利亚将克服安全挑战，并敦促青年继续相信国家未来，同时支持恢复和平与稳定的努力。他说：“我总是告诉他们，今天你们看到的魔鬼，很快就会再也见不到。很快，我们就会克服当前面临的不安全局势。因此，你们四处开展竞选活动时，务必保持信心。”

Akpabio 坚持认为，权力下放式警务将进一步强化国家安全，尤其是提升执法机构应对各自社区内威胁的能力。他敦促 Arewa 青年在2027年总统选举前动员支持 Tinubu，并表示本届政府需要时间巩固各项政策。

他说，总统已经采取措施，使尼日利亚摆脱长期以来对原油收入的依赖，并推行旨在重塑经济地位的改革。他说：“我期待尼日利亚青年能够超越社交媒体上的宣传，因为这位总统已经带领我们摆脱单一经济，也就是一种只依赖原油的经济。”

Akpabio 表示，本届政府的表现赢得了国民议会的支持，并宣称议员们已经支持 Tinubu 连任。他说：“自独立以来，还没有哪位总统在这个国家取得他今天所达到的发展水平。唱反调者不愿承认这一点，但我非常自豪，国民议会成员也都非常自豪。”

Akpabio 表示，尼日利亚在经济与安全困境中依然存续，体现了总统愿意正面应对国家所面临挑战的决心。他说：“我感谢上帝，尼日利亚依然存续，而且之所以能够存续，是因为我们拥有一位会思考、愿意面对挑战的总统，而他正在迎接这些挑战。”

他敦促青年支持政府延续执政，并表示，如果在本届政府政策尚未完全成熟之前更迭政府，就可能削弱迄今取得的进展。他说：“不要更换一支正在获胜的队伍。他的表现如此出色。让他的政策充分成型。这不是一个前来试验的人。他已经在付诸实践。”

Akpabio 还强调青年参与国家发展的重要性，表示政府政策应为后代建立稳定的基础。他说：“我们今天所做的一切，都是为了让你们的未来更加稳定，并确保尼日利亚得以存续。因此，你们现在看到这些成果是好事。”

他警告称，青年在反驳社交媒体上对本届政府的批评时可能面临巨大困难，并指称一些在网上攻击总统及其支持者的人正因此获得报酬。Akpabio 指控说：“这对你们来说不会容易，因为大多数在社交媒体上攻击总统和这些年轻人的人都是拿钱办事。而你们没有拿钱。”

他建议青年定期组织基层交流活动，解释政府政策并反驳错误信息，而不是试图在社交媒体上持续与批评者竞争。他说：“你们或许无法投入他们那样的精力和时间。但可以偶尔召集青年，让大家看到真相、认识真相。”

此次拜访让 Arewa Revival Project 有机会表达对 Akpabio 领导国民议会的支持，并认可其所称的 Akpabio 对国家发展的贡献。此前，Arewa Revival Project 项目协调员 Hon. Mustafa Ibrahim 表示，该组织认为 Akpabio 对国家建设作出的贡献，以及其在领导国民议会期间取得的成就，足以令其获得表彰。这个成员遍及北部19个州的团体向参议院议长颁发了奖项，以表彰他对国家发展的贡献。
