https://leadership.ng/kano-kogi-pass-sta.body: The Kano and Kogi State Houses of Assembly have passed the bill seeking an alteration of the 1999 Constitution to provide for the establishment of state police. The passage comes amid ongoing efforts to amend the Constitution to allow states to establish their own police services. The Kano State House of Assembly passed the bill alongside a supplementary appropriation and amendment bill of N1.21 trillion. The bills were passed during Tuesday’s plenary presided over by the Speaker, Isma’il Falgore, after consideration by the Committee of the Whole and passage through third reading. The state police bill, which seeks to amend the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, was considered clause by clause from one to 26 before it was passed by the lawmakers. The Assembly also passed the Kano State Supplementary Appropriation and Amendment Bill, 2026, reducing the earlier request of the state from N1.478 trillion to approximately N1.211 trillion. The adjustment represents a reduction of about N266.61 billion from the original budget of N1,477,829,666,130.71. The supplementary budget followed a proposal transmitted to the Assembly by Governor Abba Yusuf for legislative consideration and approval. The Kogi State House of Assembly unanimously passed the proposed constitutional amendment for the establishment of state police, citing the need to strengthen internal security, improve emergency response and create employment opportunities for youths. The Speaker of the House, Aliyu Umar Yusuf, disclosed this during plenary deliberations on the Constitution Alteration Bill seeking to establish state police across the country. Yusuf described the consideration of the bill as a significant legislative milestone, noting that it provided the Assembly with an opportunity to contribute to the national discourse on improving the protection of lives and property. He said the growing incidence of terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, farmer-herder conflicts, political thuggery and other criminal activities had underscored the need to explore additional measures to address the country’s security challenges. According to him, the increasing complexity of security threats requires a more decentralised policing structure that would enable states to respond swiftly to security concerns within their jurisdictions. The Speaker recalled that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had proposed the constitutional amendment to the National Assembly, where it was considered and passed by both chambers before being transmitted to state Houses of Assembly for consideration and voting in accordance with Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. He explained that state police would enable state governments to recruit personnel familiar with their local communities and the peculiar security challenges confronting them. Such personnel, he said, would be better positioned to gather intelligence, identify suspicious movements and respond promptly to distress calls, thereby complementing the operations of the Nigeria Police Force. Yusuf added that decentralising policing would reduce administrative bottlenecks and improve operational efficiency, particularly in communities requiring urgent security intervention. He also identified employment generation as another potential benefit of the proposed arrangement, noting that the recruitment of young people into state police formations could help address unemployment and its associated social challenges. Contributing to the debate, lawmakers expressed support for the proposed amendment, arguing that state police would bring security operations closer to the people and facilitate quicker responses to emergencies. They maintained that recruiting personnel from local communities would enhance intelligence gathering, as officers familiar with their environments would be better equipped to identify unfamiliar persons and movements that could pose security threats. The lawmakers further argued that state police would help curb criminal activities and strengthen the existing federal policing structure, which they described as overstretched by its responsibilities across the country. Yusuf urged his colleagues to support the bill, stressing that their decision would demonstrate the Assembly’s commitment to public safety, effective governance and the search for lasting solutions to Nigeria’s security challenges. He said the proposed amendment offered Kogi State an opportunity to contribute to the development of a more effective security framework capable of addressing emerging threats. The Speaker added that supporting the bill would demonstrate the lawmakers’ readiness to embrace reforms aimed at tackling persistent insecurity. At the end of deliberations, the Assembly unanimously passed the bill and directed the Clerk of the House to communicate its decision to the National Assembly. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/kano-kogi-pass-sta.title_zh: 卡诺州和科吉州通过州警察法案
https://leadership.ng/kano-kogi-pass-sta.body_zh:
卡诺州和科吉州议会已通过一项法案，拟修改1999年《宪法》，规定设立州警察。此举是在各方持续推动修宪、允许各州建立本州警察服务的背景下作出的。卡诺州议会通过该法案的同时，还通过了一项金额为1.21万亿奈拉（₦）的补充拨款及修正案法案。周二全体会议由议长Isma’il Falgore主持，相关法案经全体委员会审议并完成三读后获得通过。该州警察法案旨在修改《尼日利亚联邦共和国1999年宪法》，议员逐条审议了第1至第26条，随后表决通过。议会还通过了《2026年卡诺州补充拨款及修正案法案》，将该州最初提出的1.478万亿奈拉拨款削减至约1.211万亿奈拉。此次调整使原始预算1,477,829,666,130.71奈拉减少约266.61亿奈拉。补充预算源于州长Abba Yusuf提交议会审议和批准的提案。

科吉州议会一致通过了一项关于设立州警察的拟议宪法修正案，并表示此举是加强国内安全、改进紧急响应以及为青年创造就业机会所必需的。州议会议长Aliyu Umar Yusuf在审议旨在全国各地设立州警察的《宪法修正案法案》时透露了上述决定。Yusuf称，审议该法案是一项重大的立法里程碑，使议会得以参与改善生命和财产保护的全国性讨论。他说，恐怖主义、武装劫掠、绑架、农牧民冲突、政治暴徒及其他犯罪活动日益频发，表明尼日利亚有必要探索更多措施，应对国家面临的安全挑战。据他介绍，日益复杂的安全威胁要求建立更加分权的治安体系，使各州能够迅速应对其管辖范围内的安全问题。议长回顾称，总统Bola Ahmed Tinubu已向国民议会提出宪法修正案，该修正案经两院审议并通过后，依照经修订的1999年《宪法》第9条移交各州议会审议和表决。他解释说，州警察将使州政府能够招募熟悉当地社区及本地特殊安全挑战的人员。他说，这些人员将更有条件收集情报、识别可疑动向并迅速响应求救电话，从而配合尼日利亚警察部队开展行动。Yusuf还指出，推动治安权力下放将减少行政瓶颈、提高行动效率，尤其是在亟需安全干预的社区。他还认为，创造就业是拟议安排的另一项潜在益处，因为招募青年加入州警察队伍有助于缓解失业及其带来的社会问题。

议员们在讨论中表示支持拟议修正案，认为州警察将使安全行动更贴近民众，并加快对紧急事件的响应。他们坚持认为，从当地社区招募人员将增强情报收集能力，因为熟悉环境的警员更有能力识别可能构成安全威胁的陌生人员和动向。议员们还指出，州警察将有助于遏制犯罪活动，并加强现有联邦警务体系；他们称，该体系承担全国范围内的职责，目前已不堪重负。Yusuf敦促同僚支持该法案，强调他们的决定将体现州议会对公共安全、有效治理以及寻求持久解决尼日利亚安全挑战的承诺。他说，拟议修正案为科吉州提供了参与制定更有效安全框架的机会，以应对新出现的威胁。议长补充称，支持该法案将表明议员们愿意接受旨在解决持续存在的不安全问题的改革。

全体会议审议结束后，议会一致通过该法案，并指示议会秘书将决定通报国民议会。我们掌握前沿动态。获取实时报道、独家爆料和深入视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp频道，随时随地接收24/7最新消息→

https://leadership.ng/federal-govt-appro.summary_zh: 联邦政府批准自2026年11月起，连续6个月向公共服务系统各级工作人员每月发放N70,000交通补贴。虽然N70,000的每月交通补贴将从11月起实施6个月，但各项特殊津贴欠款将从同月起分3期等额支付。
https://leadership.ng/federal-govt-appro.body: The federal government has approved a monthly transport intervention of N70,000 for workers across all levels of the public service for six months, beginning from November 2026. The decision followed an agreement reached with organised labour over rising living costs and outstanding workers’ welfare demands. The agreement was reached yesterday at a meeting between the federal government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. Under the agreement, payment of arrears of the approved peculiar allowance will also begin in November and be completed in three equal monthly instalments. The meeting further resolved that the National Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted immediately and commence work, although both parties disagreed over the effective date for implementing the outcome of the negotiations. The meeting, convened by the Minister of Labour and Employment, Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi, followed an earlier round of talks on October 22 to address concerns raised by organised labour. Those who signed the agreement on behalf of the federal government included the Director-General of the Budget Office, Tanimu Yakubu; the Permanent Secretary, Service Welfare Office, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Garba Abdul S.U.; and Dingyadi, who served as conciliator. The labour delegation was represented by the NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the National Secretary of the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council (JNPSNC), Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo. The agreement stated that the federal government had approved the peculiar allowance with effect from May 1, 2026, with payment of outstanding arrears scheduled to commence in November. The parties also agreed that 19 months of outstanding allowances owed to health workers would be paid within three months, beginning in December 2026. On the demand for hazard allowance for agricultural officers, the meeting noted that the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security had submitted the list of beneficiaries and the associated financial implications to the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission (NSIWC) for verification. The verification is expected to be completed within two weeks, after which the commission will issue an implementation template. Regarding the adjustment of the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS), the NSIWC is expected to update the cost implications within three weeks to enable the Presidential Committee on Salaries to make a decision. The demand for tax relief for workers was referred to the NLC’s National Executive Council, with the meeting noting that taxation was a statutory matter. The parties also urged state and local governments to participate in the intervention process and called on labour unions to press for the implementation of the resolutions. On the minimum wage negotiations, the resolutions stated: “It was agreed that the Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee would be constituted and to commence meeting immediately. It should, however, be noted that there is a disagreement on the effective date of implementation.” On the peculiar allowance, it stated: “The peculiar allowance has been approved by the Federal Government effective from 1 May 2026. The payment of the arrears would commence in November, 2026 in three equal monthly instalments.” The key resolutions, therefore, cover the transport intervention, payment of outstanding allowances, the proposed minimum wage negotiations and the review of other workers’ welfare issues. While the N70,000 monthly transport intervention will run for six months from November, peculiar allowance arrears will be paid in three equal instalments beginning the same month. The 19 months of outstanding allowances owed to health workers are to be cleared within three months from December. The government is also expected to complete verification of agricultural officers’ hazard allowance within two weeks and update the cost implications of the CONHESS adjustment within three weeks. Meanwhile, the proposed minimum wage negotiations are expected to begin immediately after the committee is constituted, although the parties have yet to agree on the effective date for implementing the outcome. The demand for tax relief remains subject to consideration by the NLC’s National Executive Council. Both parties agreed to reconvene after one month to assess implementation of the resolutions. LEADERSHIP reported that the NLC had issued a two-week ultimatum to the federal government on October 9, demanding the commencement of negotiations on a new national minimum wage, a reduction in petrol pump prices, palliatives for workers and the resolution of outstanding public service welfare issues. The ultimatum expired on October 22 without a breakthrough, prompting organised labour to set October 27 as a fresh deadline for meaningful progress. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/federal-govt-appro.title_zh: 联邦政府批准每月向劳动者提供7万奈拉交通补贴
https://leadership.ng/federal-govt-appro.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府批准，自2026年11月起，连续6个月向各级公共服务部门工作人员每月发放N70,000交通补贴。该决定是联邦政府与有组织劳工就生活成本上涨及尚未落实的职工福利诉求达成协议后作出的。协议于昨日在联邦政府与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）领导层于联邦劳工与就业部举行的会议上达成。根据协议，已获批准的特定津贴欠款也将从11月开始支付，并在3个月内分3期等额付清。会议还决定立即组建全国最低工资谈判委员会并开始工作，但双方对谈判结果实施生效的日期存在分歧。此次会议由劳工与就业部长Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi召集，是继10月22日 earlier一轮旨在处理有组织劳工所提关切的会谈后举行的。代表联邦政府签署协议的人员包括预算办公室主任Tanimu Yakabu、联邦公务员事务首长办公室服务福利办公室常任秘书Garba Abdul S.U.，以及担任调解人的Dingyadi。劳工代表团由NLC主席Comrade Joe Ajaero和全国公共服务联合谈判委员会（JNPSNC）全国书记Comrade Gbenga Olowoyo代表。协议称，联邦政府已批准特定津贴，自2026年5月1日起生效，欠款计划从11月开始支付。双方还同意，欠付医务人员的19个月津贴将在3个月内付清，从2026年12月开始。关于要求为农业官员发放危险津贴的诉求，会议 noted 联邦农业与粮食安全部已将受益人名单及相关财务影响提交全国薪金、收入与工资委员会（NSIWC）核查。预计核查将在2周内完成，随后委员会将发布实施模板。关于调整《综合卫生薪金结构》（CONHESS），预计NSIWC将在3周内更新成本影响测算，以便总统薪金委员会作出决定。有关为工作人员减税的诉求被提交NLC全国执行委员会审议，会议指出，税收属于法定事项。双方还敦促州和地方政府参与补贴发放进程，并呼吁工会推动相关决议的落实。关于最低工资谈判，决议指出：“双方同意立即组建最低工资谈判委员会并开始会议。但需要指出的是，双方对实施生效日期存在分歧。”关于特定津贴，决议指出：“联邦政府已批准特定津贴，自2026年5月1日起生效。欠款将从2026年11月开始支付，分3期等额按月支付。”因此，主要决议涵盖交通补贴发放、拖欠津贴支付、拟议最低工资谈判以及其他职工福利问题的审查。N70,000的月度交通补贴将从11月起实施6个月，特定津贴欠款也将从同月开始分3期等额支付。欠付医务人员的19个月津贴须自12月起在3个月内付清。政府预计将在2周内完成农业官员危险津贴的核查，并在3周内更新CONHESS调整的成本影响测算。与此同时，拟议的最低工资谈判预计将在委员会组建后立即开始，但双方尚未就谈判结果实施生效的日期达成一致。减税诉求仍待NLC全国执行委员会审议。双方同意在1个月后再次会面，评估各项决议的落实情况。LEADERSHIP报道称，NLC于10月9日向联邦政府发出为期两周的最后通牒，要求启动新的全国最低工资谈判、降低加油站油价、为工作人员提供纾困措施，并解决尚未落实的公共服务福利问题。最后通牒于10月22日到期，但未取得突破，促使有组织劳工将10月27日设为取得实质性进展的新期限。我们掌握独家视角。实时报道、独家内幕和独家分析将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候更新 →

https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102802.body: (서울=연합뉴스) 정회인 기자 = 하나증권은 28일 유럽연합(EU)이 중국산 타이어에 대한 관세를 강화하면서 중국 공장에서 생산해 유럽으로 수출하는 국내 타이어 업체들의 비용 부담도 커질 것으로 전망했다. EU는 지난 7월 중국산 승용차·경트럭용 타이어에 4.3∼45.3%의 반덤핑 관세를 확정한 데 이어 최근 정부 보조금을 이유로 한 상계관세 판정안도 공개한 것으로 알려졌다. 최종 관세율은 의견 수렴을 거쳐 12월 초 확정될 예정이다. EU 집행위원회도 지난 7월 반덤핑 관세를 확정하면서 같은 품목에 대한 반보조금 조사가 별도로 진행 중이며 연내 마무리될 예정이라고 밝힌 바 있다. 하나증권 송선재 연구원은 이날 보고서에서 "국내 타이어 3사가 중국 공장에서 생산해 EU로 수출하는 물량에도 반덤핑 관세와 상계관세가 부과된다"고 설명했다. 판정안대로 확정될 경우 총 관세율은 한국타이어가 27.5%, 금호타이어[073240]와 넥센타이어[002350]가 각각 28.76%가 된다. 특히 기존 관세율이 4.3%에 불과했던 한국타이어의 부담은 23.2%포인트(p) 높아지는 반면 금호타이어와 넥센타이어는 각각 4.4%포인트 상승한다. 이에 따라 3사 간 관세율 격차도 기존 20.1%포인트에서 1.3%포인트로 좁혀진다. 다만 실제 이익 부담은 업체별 중국 생산 비중에 따라 다를 것으로 봤다. 하나증권이 추정한 내년 관세 비용은 한국타이어 1천490억원, 금호타이어 1천440억원, 넥센타이어 160억원이다. 영업이익 대비 부담은 중국산 비중이 높은 금호타이어의 비중이 22%로 가장 높고, 넥센타이어 8%, 한국타이어 6% 순이다. 송 연구원은 "3사 모두 생산지 재배치로 중국산 비중을 낮출 계획"이라며 "당사 가정보다 빠르게 낮춘다면 관세 비용은 더 줄어들 수 있다"고 설명했다. 이어 "판가 전가와 중국 업체의 저가 공세 약화에 따른 가격 환경 개선도 부담을 일부 상쇄할 수 있다"고 덧붙였다. 하나증권은 관세 부담에 따른 이익 추정치 하향을 반영해 한국타이어 목표주가를 8만5천원에서 8만원으로 낮췄다. 넥센타이어도 원가 상승 등을 반영해 목표주가를 1만500원에서 8천400원으로 하향했고, 금호타이어는 기존 반덤핑 관세 부담을 이미 실적에 반영했다며 7천700원을 유지했다. 세 종목에 대한 투자의견은 모두 '매수'다. 제보는 카카오톡 okjebo <저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포, AI 학습 및 활용 금지> 2026/10/28 08:24 송고 2026년10월28일 08시24분 송고
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102802.title_zh: Hana证券：“欧盟加强对中国轮胎的关税……韩国企业负担加重”
https://www.yna.co.kr/view/akr2026102802.body_zh: （首尔=联合新闻）郑慧仁记者=随着欧盟28日加强对中国产轮胎征收关税，在中国工厂生产并向欧洲出口的韩国轮胎企业预计也将承担更高的成本。据悉，欧盟继7月确定对中国产乘用车和轻型卡车轮胎征收4.3%至45.3%的反倾销税后，近期又因政府补贴问题公布了征收反补贴税的裁定方案。最终税率将在汇总各方意见后于12月初确定。欧盟执行委员会也在7月确定反倾销税时表示，针对同一产品的反补贴调查正在单独进行，预计年内完成。Hana证券研究员宋善宰当天在报告中解释道：“韩国3家轮胎企业从中国工厂生产并向欧盟出口的轮胎，也将被征收反倾销税和反补贴税。”如果按裁定方案确定，总税率将分别为韩国轮胎27.5%、锦湖轮胎[073240]和耐克森轮胎[002350]各28.76%。尤其是韩国轮胎现行税率仅为4.3%，税负将提高23.2个百分点（p）；锦湖轮胎和耐克森轮胎则各上升4.4个百分点。3家企业的税率差距也将从原来的20.1个百分点缩小至1.3个百分点。不过，实际利润负担预计将因各企业中国生产占比不同而有所差异。Hana证券估算的明年关税成本分别为韩国轮胎1490亿韩元、锦湖轮胎1440亿韩元、耐克森轮胎160亿韩元。相对于营业利润，负担占比最高的是中国产占比最高的锦湖轮胎，为22%；耐克森轮胎为8%；韩国轮胎为6%。宋研究员表示：“3家企业均计划通过重新配置生产基地来降低中国产占比。如果下降速度超过预期，关税成本可能进一步减少。”他补充道：“随着价格向产品转移，以及中国厂商通过低税率削弱价格优势，价格环境改善也可能抵消部分负担。”Hana证券反映关税负担导致的盈利预估下调，将韩国轮胎目标股价从8.5万韩元下调至8万韩元。耐克森轮胎也因成本上升等因素，将目标股价从1.5万韩元下调至8400韩元；锦湖轮胎因既有反倾销税负担已反映在业绩中，维持7700韩元不变。对这3只股票的投资评级均为“买入”。举报可通过KakaoTalk联系okjebo <版权所有(c) 联合新闻，未经许可禁止转载、复制发行，禁止用于人工智能训练及使用> 2026/10/28 08:24发稿 2026年10月28日08时24分发稿

https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/404291268066291.body: CNCEC's subsidiary signs a low-margin photovoltaic EPC contract in Ghana, testing payment collection capability and project execution capacity. According to the announcement of CNCEC, its subsidiary Sedin Engineering has signed a 300MW photovoltaic EPC contract in Ghana. Four Chinese companies, three West African countries, four completely different market entry strategies. The RMB 2.58 billion deal of CNCEC is the largest among them and the closest to the traditional centralized EPC model. However, it is facing a market where the government has cut the electricity price from 18 cents to 6.5 cents, independent power producers' arrears are still accumulating, and the gross profit margin of photovoltaic EPC has been compressed to a single-digit range. Can an engineering company with a background in coal chemical industry and advanced chemical new materials find its own position in the low-margin photovoltaic sector in West Africa? By the end of 2025, Ghana's cumulative installed photovoltaic capacity reached 276.7MW, of which utility-scale capacity was only 183.1MW, lower than the previously set target of 347.5MW. The updated 2026-2030 plan sets the new ground-mounted photovoltaic target at 852MW, which will be equipped with nearly 2GWh of battery energy storage, and the private sector will undertake 41% of the utility-scale photovoltaic investment. The 300MW single project volume of Sedin exceeds 1.6 times the existing utility-scale photovoltaic stock in Ghana. The figures on the demand side are clear, and even a little urgent. But on the payment side opposite the demand, there is a completely different logic. The Electricity Company of Ghana collects electricity bills in Ghanaian cedi and pays independent power producers in US dollars. Every time the cedi weakens, arrears return to the accounts receivable of independent power producers in the way of "re-accumulation". The Ghanaian Minister of Energy disclosed in October 2026 that the monthly payment ratio to IPPs has increased from about 40% to nearly 100%. The Minister of Finance said that the 2026 budget has allocated 345 million US dollars for energy payments, with the goal of "no new arrears accumulated for the first time". These improvements are real, but they are also political commitments. For an EPC contract with a construction period of two to three years, the sustainability of the commitment is more worthy of attention than the intensity of the commitment. As the EPC contractor, Sedin does not hold the power station assets and does not directly bear the erosion of the cedi depreciation on electricity bill income. However, the release of its progress payment and quality guarantee deposit depends on the rhythm of the owner receiving money from the power purchaser. When the cash flow of the power purchaser is squeezed by the exchange rate, the payment milestones in the EPC contract will be extended first. Low price is not the biggest problem, but the opaque payment path is. In the first half of 2026, CNCEC signed new overseas contracts of 72.935 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 76%, and the proportion of overseas revenue rose to 35%; in the first 8 months, the new overseas contracts signed reached 79.188 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 57.46%. In emerging tracks such as photovoltaic and energy storage, the company's expression is to "continue to make efforts". The most notable public track record of Sedin in the field of photovoltaic EPC is the 150MW DC project in Laos signed in 2025, with a contract value of 528 million yuan, less than half the scale of the Ghana project. The span from 150MW to 300MW, from Southeast Asia to West Africa, from chemical plants to ground-mounted power stations is obvious. Within the CNCEC system, Hualu Company has long-term accumulation in the engineering of polysilicon materials. The multi-professional interface management, long-cycle equipment procurement rhythm control and overseas on-site construction organization trained by chemical EPC have a considerable proportion of reuse space in ground-mounted photovoltaic power stations. The problem is that what is reused is engineering discipline, not profit thickness. The reason why the gross profit margin of chemical EPC is higher than that of ordinary civil engineering is that the process complexity forms an entry barrier; the process barrier of photovoltaic EPC is much thinner, and the competitors are much denser. If Sedin's 0.86 yuan/W corresponds to a power station body with compressed boundaries, the price is not as aggressive as it seems on the surface; if it corresponds to a more complete scope of work, the profit margin will be further squeezed. The 2.58 billion yuan Ghana project accounts for about 2.6% of CNCEC's total new overseas contracts signed in the first three quarters of 2026, and will not change the overall profit direction alone. But it is a verification sample: Can Sedin turn photovoltaic EPC in Ghana from a one-time "new track breakthrough" into a repeatable business category. If it can, there will be negotiation chips for the second and third projects in West Africa; if not, the 2.58 billion yuan will only be a nice-looking announcement. Looking at the bigger picture, Sedin is not the only Chinese enterprise placing bets in West Africa, but its playstyle is clearly different when compared with several other peers. Sedin's position is heavier than Sungrow's, and lighter than China Energy Engineering's centralized EPC. It does not only earn profits from the manufacturing end like JinkoSolar, nor does it bind the national power company in Senegal to do a 500MW framework like China Energy Engineering. It is taking on a low-margin photovoltaic general contracting project with chemical engineering discipline in a market where electricity prices have been renegotiated and payments are being restored but not yet stable. Sedin's 2.58 billion yuan has bought a ticket to enter the African new energy EPC table. It has already sat at the table. The heaviest chip on the table is not the quotation, but the payment calendar of the Electricity Company of Ghana and who will stand in front of the contractor when the cedi fluctuates next time. https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/404291268066291.body_zh: 中国化学旗下子公司在加纳签署低利润率光伏EPC合同，检验回款能力和项目执行能力。据中国化学公告，其子公司塞丁工程已在加纳签署一座300MW光伏EPC合同。4家中资企业、3个西非国家、4种截然不同的市场进入策略。中国化学这笔25.8亿元人民币的交易是其中规模最大的一笔，也最接近传统的集权式EPC模式。然而，该项目面临的市场环境十分严峻：加纳政府已将电价从18美分下调至6.5美分，独立发电商的欠款仍在累积，光伏EPC的毛利率已被压缩至个位数区间。一家拥有煤化工和先进化工新材料背景的工程公司，能否在西非低利润率光伏领域找到自己的位置？截至2025年底，加纳累计光伏装机容量达到276.7MW，其中公用事业规模装机仅为183.1MW，低于此前设定的347.5MW目标。更新后的2026—2030年计划将新建地面光伏目标设定为852MW，并配套近2GWh电池储能，其中私营部门将承担公用事业规模光伏投资的41%。塞丁300MW单体项目的规模超过加纳现有公用事业规模光伏装机的1.6倍。需求端的数据十分清晰，甚至已有些迫切。但与需求端相对，付款端遵循的是一套完全不同的逻辑。加纳电力公司以加纳塞地收取电费，再以美元向独立发电商付款。每当塞地走弱，独立发电商的欠款就会以“重新累积”的方式回到应收账款中。加纳能源部长于2026年10月披露，向独立发电商按月支付的比例已从约40%提高至接近100%。财政部长表示，2026年预算已安排3.45亿美元用于能源付款，目标是“首次不再新增欠款”。这些改善是真实存在的，但同样属于政治承诺。对于建设期为两至三年的EPC合同而言，承诺能否持续比承诺的力度更值得关注。作为EPC承包商，塞丁不持有电站资产，也不直接承受塞地贬值侵蚀电费收入的影响。然而，其进度款和质量保证金的释放取决于业主从购电方收到资金的节奏。当购电方的现金流受到汇率挤压时，EPC合同的付款节点将首先被延后。低价并非最大问题，不透明的付款路径才是。2026年上半年，中国化学新签海外合同729.35亿元，同比增长76%，海外收入占比升至35%；前8个月新签海外合同额达到791.88亿元，同比增长57.46%。在光伏、储能等新兴赛道上，该公司的表述是“继续努力”。塞丁在光伏EPC领域最引人注目的公开业绩，是2025年签署的老挝150MW直流项目，合同金额5.28亿元，不到加纳项目规模的一半。从150MW到300MW，从东南亚到西非，从化工装置到地面电站，各方面的跨越十分明显。在中国化学体系内，华陆公司长期积累的多晶硅材料工程经验具有较高复用价值。化工EPC所形成的多专业接口管理、长周期设备采购节奏控制和海外现场施工组织能力，在地面光伏电站中也有相当大的复用空间。问题在于，复用的是工程纪律，而非利润厚度。化工EPC毛利率高于普通土建工程，是因为工艺复杂度形成了进入壁垒；光伏EPC的工艺壁垒要薄得多，竞争者也密集得多。如果塞丁的0.86元/W对应的是边界被压缩的电站主体，那么这个价格表面上并没有看上去那么激进；如果对应的是更完整的承包范围，利润率还将进一步受到挤压。加纳25.8亿元项目约占中国化学2026年前三季度新签海外合同总额的2.6%，单凭该项目不会改变整体利润走势。但这依然是一个验证样本：塞丁能否把加纳光伏EPC从一次性“新赛道突破”变成可复制的业务品类？如果可以，塞丁在承接西非第二、第三个项目时就掌握了谈判筹码；如果不能，25.8亿元只会是一则好看的公告。放眼全局，押注西非的中国企业并非只有塞丁，但与其他几家同行相比，它的打法明显不同。塞丁的定位比阳光电源更重，又比中国能源建设的集权式EPC更轻。它既不像晶科 solar 那样主要从制造端获利，也不像中国能源建设那样将塞内加尔国家电力公司绑定于500MW框架协议。它是在电价经过重新谈判、付款正在恢复但尚未稳定的市场中，以化工工程的严谨标准承接低利润率光伏总承包项目。塞丁的25.8亿元为其买入了一张进入非洲新能源EPC牌桌的入场券，而它已经坐在了牌桌前。牌桌上最重的筹码不是报价，而是加纳电力公司的付款日程，以及下一次塞地波动时谁会站在承包商前面。中国化学的化工产业基础能够帮助塞丁建设电站，但工程完工后的资金能否沿着从塞地到美元的路径顺利收回，取决于合同结构中是否有相应安排，能够为承包商屏蔽汇率风险。36kr Europe（eu.36kr.com）向全球提供商业和市场新闻、数据、分析及视频，致力于助力企业全球拓展并创造价值、提供商业服务

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title: How ONSA under Dasuki paid out security funds received from CBN, accountant general
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: A bank official on Tuesday gave details of security funds the Sambo Dasuki-led Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) received from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation in 2015, and how the funds were transferred to various beneficiaries. Going through the statement of the ONSA’s account on Tuesday, the witness informed the court that the former NSA, Mr Dasuki, and one Salisu Abdulmalik Shaibu used to be signatories to the account with Access Bank.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 一名银行官员周二详细说明了由桑博·达苏基担任国家安全顾问的办公室（ONSA）于2015年从尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）和联邦总审计长办公室收到的安全资金，以及这些资金如何转拨给各类受益人。证人在周二查看 ONSA 账户对账单后向法院表示，前国家安全顾问达苏基先生和一名名叫萨利苏·阿卜杜勒马利克·谢布的人曾是 Access Bank 账户的签字人。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: A bank official on Tuesday gave details of security funds the Sambo Dasuki-led Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) received from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation in 2015, and how the funds were transferred to various beneficiaries. Arhyel Mshelia, a compliance officer with Access Bank, testified before the FCT High Court in Maitama as the third prosecution witness in an over-a-decade-long N4.6 billion arms procurement fraud trial case involving Mr Dasuki. Mr Mshelia narrated how the security funds made their ways into the accounts of Jabbama Ada Global Services, Jawas Multipurpose Ventures and Onile Nigeria Limited in 2015. Mr Dasuki has been standing trial in the case since 2015 alongside former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited. Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants are facing 25 counts of misappropriation, criminal breach of trust and receiving stolen property. The charges accuse them of diverting N4.6 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists during former President Goodluck Jonathan administration, between 2014 and 2015. Going through the statement of the ONSA’s account on Tuesday, the witness informed the court that the former NSA, Mr Dasuki, and one Salisu Abdulmalik Shaibu used to be signatories to the account with Access Bank. Arhyel said on 16 March 2015, there was an inflow credit of N500 million from the CBN; the amount was disbursed on 25 March, 2015. Similarly, the account was credited with N5 billion on 10 April 2015. On 16 April 2015, N27 million and N400 million were sent to Jabbama Ada Global Limited. The signatory to Jabbama Ada was Salisu Umar Garu, the witness said. He also said Jabbama Ada received N500 million on 5 February 2015 and N1 billion on 16 April 2015 from the ONSA’s office. From the Federation Allocation Account Committee’s (FAAC’s) account with the OAGF, the company received N38 million and N25 million on 6 and 7 January 2015, respectively and N55 million on 5 February 2015. According to the witness, Onile Nigeria Limited, whose signatory is Tom Ikimi, received N200 million and N100 million from ONSA on 9 and 18 February 2015. Jawas Multipurpose Ventures also received N2 billion, he said. During cross-examination by the defence, the witness said he did not know the purpose of the transactions. He also disclosed that Jabbama Ada was involved in general contracts, oil and gas, purchase and resale of lands and transport. Fielding questions from Mr Yuguda and Dalhatu Investment Limited’s lawyer, James Olatoke, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), the witness said he did not know of any relationship between Jabbama Ada and his clients. He also noted transfers from other individuals and companies aside from the ONSA and CBN. The first prosecution witness, Hamza Abdullahi, who served as the second-in-command of the EFCC’s Special Task Force that investigated the alleged arms procurement fraud in the NSA office, had testified that N4.633 billion was traced to Dalhatu Investment Limited. He said Mr Sagir, the son of the former Sokoto governor, is the company’s sole account signatory. The second prosecution witness, Mr Yusuf, had also testified that funds were released from the NSA office for the supply of security equipment but that the contracts were not executed. He said that during the investigation, Mr Sagir brought a list showing how the funds were used. The witness said the funds were used to sponsor pilgrimage to Mecca and partly used for the 2015 political campaigns of the then-ruling party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He listed the recipients of the funds to include Sheikh AbdurRahman Al-Sudais Foundation (N500 million), belonging to former Governor Bafarawa, and 2015 Sokoto PDP governorship candidate, Abdallah Wali, who allegedly received N580 million through a company. The case is one of the twin arms procurement fraud matters filed against Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants over the streams of funds he released from NSA office accounts between 2014 and 2015. In the other trial, the EFCC is prosecuting Mr Dasuki, a retired colonel, alongside a former General Manager at the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), Aminu Baba-Kusa; Acacia Holdings Limited; and Reliance Referral Hospital Limited on 32 counts of fraud involving diversion of N33.2 billion arms funds entrusted to the NSA office. In March, the EFCC re-arraigned the defendants on criminal breach of trust, among other charges, following the reassignment of the case that started in 2015 to a new judge, Charles Agbaza. The defendants denied all charges as they did when they were first arraigned in 2015. The two cases suffered multiple adjournments in their early years, largely due to the State Security Services (SSS) refusing to release Mr Dasuki on bail despite multiple court orders. Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, at the height of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, during the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan. An audit panel set up by the administration of President Muhammadu Buhari, who came to office after defeating Mr Jonathan in the 2015 presidential election, revealed that about $2 billion entrusted to the office of the NSA, then led by Mr Dasuki, for procurement of arms could not be accounted for. The EFCC, which instituted multiple charges against diverse persons who received funds from the NSA office, alleged that the arms funds were doled out to friends, relatives, political allies, particularly members of the PDP, for purposes unrelated to the purchase of arms

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to establish a transparent framework for the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and other clean mobility equipment into Nigeria. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 众议院已呼吁联邦政府为电动汽车、压缩天然气车辆及其他清洁出行设备进口至尼日利亚建立透明框架。他敦促联邦政府为电动汽车、压缩天然气车辆及相关清洁出行设备的商业进口建立透明的许可和审批框架。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to establish a transparent framework for the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and other clean mobility equipment into Nigeria. The call followed a motion moved by Ademorin Kuye (APC, Lagos) during Tuesday’s plenary in Abuja. Moving the motion, Mr Kuye said Nigeria has adopted policies that promote the transition to EVs, CNG vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, and other clean transportation technologies as part of its energy transition and economic diversification agenda. He said the government had introduced fiscal incentives, including import duty and tax reliefs, to encourage investment in clean mobility technologies and expand charging infrastructure and CNG refuelling stations. He said the policy’s success would also depend on the availability of maintenance centres, spare parts, technical expertise, and after-sales support. Mr Kuye said Nigeria could use the import incentives to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation and domestic value addition by linking the incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity. “Nigeria has the opportunity to encourage local investment, technology transfer, employment generation, and domestic value addition by linking import incentives to measurable investments in infrastructure and technical capacity,” he said. He urged the federal government to establish a transparent licensing and approval framework for the commercial importation of EVs, CNG vehicles and related clean mobility equipment. He also urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and other relevant agencies, to develop objective criteria for approving importers. Under the proposed framework, companies seeking approval would, where applicable, be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technical personnel. They would also be required to invest in EV charging infrastructure or CNG refuelling facilities, comply with Nigerian safety, environmental and technical standards, and submit consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The lawmaker further urged the NADDC to maintain a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and consumer confidence. He said the approval process must remain open, competitive, and non-discriminatory, allowing any company that meets the prescribed standards to obtain approval without undue preference. He also urged the government to align tax incentives, import duty concessions, and other fiscal benefits with the proposed regulatory framework to encourage sustained investment in local infrastructure. Contributing to the debate, Dominic Okafor (APGA, Anambra) supported the motion, saying importers should be required to provide after-sales support, maintenance centres and spare parts to protect consumers. Adedeji Olajide (APM, Oyo) said greenhouse gas emissions contribute to global warming and argued that an appropriate framework for electric mobility would help Nigeria develop a more environmentally friendly transport system and contribute to global efforts to address climate change. Sada Soli (APC, Katsina) said legislation was required to provide clear guidelines for implementing the policy. The House unanimously adopted the motion after Speaker Abbas Tajudeen subjected it to a voice vote. It then asked the NADDC, BPP, SON, NCS, and other relevant agencies to develop objective qualification criteria for approving the importation of EVs, CNG vehicles, and related clean mobility equipment. The House Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment and Legislative Compliance were also mandated to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. CNG is natural gas compressed to high pressure and used as vehicle fuel. It is generally considered a cleaner-burning alternative to petrol and diesel because it produces lower levels of some pollutants and greenhouse gas emissions
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 议员要求为电动汽车和压缩天然气汽车进口建立透明框架
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 众议院敦促联邦政府为电动汽车（EV）、压缩天然气（CNG）车辆及其他清洁出行设备进口至尼日利亚建立透明框架。此项呼吁源于阿德莫林·库耶（APC，拉各斯州议员）在阿布贾星期二全体会议上提出的动议。库耶先生提出动议时表示，尼日利亚已采纳相关政策，推动向电动汽车、CNG车辆、液化石油气（LPG）车辆及其他清洁交通技术转型，作为其能源转型和经济多元化议程的一部分。他说，政府已推出财政激励措施，包括进口关税和税收减免，以鼓励对清洁出行技术的投资，并扩大充电基础设施和CNG加气站。他表示，这项政策能否成功还取决于维修中心、备件、技术专长和售后支持的可用性。库耶先生说，尼日利亚可以利用进口激励措施，通过将激励与基础设施及技术能力方面的可量化投资挂钩，鼓励本地投资、技术转让、就业创造和国内价值增值。他说：“尼日利亚有机会通过将进口激励措施与基础设施及技术能力方面的可量化投资挂钩，鼓励本地投资、技术转让、就业创造和国内价值增值。”他敦促联邦政府为商业进口电动汽车、CNG车辆及相关清洁出行设备建立透明的许可和审批框架。他还敦促国家汽车设计与开发委员会（NADDC）与公共采购局（BPP）、尼日利亚标准组织（SON）、尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）及其他相关机构合作，制定审批进口商的客观标准。根据拟议框架，申请审批的公司在适用情况下，须在尼日利亚设立经认证的服务和维修中心，提供正品备件和保修支持，并雇用和培训合格的尼日利亚技术人员。公司还须投资建设电动汽车充电基础设施或CNG加气设施，遵守尼日利亚安全、环境和技术标准，并提交消费者保护及售后服务计划。该议员进一步敦促NADDC维护获批进口商和基础设施供应商的公开名册，以促进透明度和消费者信心。他说，审批流程必须保持公开、竞争和非歧视性，使任何符合规定标准的公司都能获得审批，而不得给予不当优待。他还敦促政府使税收激励、进口关税优惠及其他财政利益与拟议监管框架相衔接，以鼓励对本地基础设施的持续投资。Dominic Okafor（APGA，阿南布拉州议员）参与讨论并支持该动议，称应要求进口商提供售后支持、维修中心和备件，以保护消费者。Adedeji Olajide（APM，奥约州议员）表示，温室气体排放会加剧全球变暖，并认为适当的电动汽车出行框架将有助于尼日利亚发展更环保的交通体系，并为全球应对气候变化的努力作出贡献。Sada Soli（APC，卡齐纳州议员）表示，需要通过立法为政策实施提供明确指引。众议院议长Abbas Tajudeen付诸表决后，表决结果为全票通过该动议。众议院随后要求NADDC、BPP、SON、NCS及其他相关机构制定审批进口电动汽车、CNG车辆及相关清洁出行设备的客观资格标准。众议院还授权工业、商业、天然气资源、环境和立法合规委员会监督政策执行情况，并在四周内提交报告，以便采取进一步立法行动。CNG是经高压压缩、用作车辆燃料的天然气。由于其产生的某些污染物和温室气体排放水平较低，通常被认为是比汽油和柴油燃烧更清洁的替代燃料

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.summary: The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system. According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.summary_zh: 总统府已责成全国有组织的私营部门制定拟议中的国家警察体系的综合融资与实施蓝图。据他介绍，私营部门与改革成败直接相关，因为不安全局势已经通过供应链中断、投资搁置、工厂扩建延期和经济机会流失，给企业带来巨大成本。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.body: The Presidency has tasked organised private sector in the country to develop a comprehensive financing and implementation blueprint for the proposed state police system. It stated that businesses must take an active role in building the security institutions required to protect investments, create jobs and strengthen economic resilience. Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, who gave the challenge, particularly charged the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), chambers of commerce and business associations with producing practical proposals for financing, institutional management and accountable partnerships to support the decentralisation of policing. According to him, the private sector has a direct stake in the success of the reform because insecurity was already imposing enormous costs on businesses through disrupted supply chains, abandoned investments, postponed factory expansions and lost economic opportunities. Speaking during a plenary session on “Security, Stability and Economic Resilience” at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, Gbajabiamila said President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to establishing state police presented an opportunity for businesses to contribute directly to the development of security institutions capable of supporting sustainable economic growth. “I therefore ask the Nigerian Economic Summit Group to carry this engagement beyond our meeting. Bring forward a considered private sector contribution on financing and implementing state police, with practical proposals for accountable partnerships. “Take that work into the legislative process and into your engagement with state governments. For our part, we remain answerable for turning reform into protection that people can rely on,” he said. Gbajabiamila urged business leaders to engage governors and legislators on the proposed reform, drawing attention to the relationship between effective local policing, employment generation and investment decisions. He explained that the experience of businesses in managing institutions, controlling expenditure and assessing risks could strengthen the design and implementation of the new policing framework. According to him, the organised private sector should also provide evidence of security failures preventing otherwise viable investments from proceeding, enabling policymakers to determine where additional security capacity was most urgently required. “His words: “Your participation should also improve the substance of the reform. As the legislative process proceeds, examine the proposals for financing and oversight. “Bring your experience of managing institutions and controlling expenditure to that discussion. Help us understand the security failures that prevent viable projects from proceeding.” The Chief of Staff, however, cautioned that private sector involvement must be transparent and should never compromise the independence of police institutions. He said businesses could contribute expertise in communications infrastructure, equipment maintenance and financial planning, but insisted that such partnerships must operate within clearly defined legal and accountability frameworks. “Where businesses provide resources, those contributions need published accounts and independent scrutiny. “Public funding must remain dependable, and a donation must never purchase influence over an investigation or preferential treatment. The object is to strengthen a public service on which every citizen can rely,” he warned. Gbajabiamila explained that the administration was determined to establish financially sustainable state police institutions, insisting that states seeking to operate their own services must demonstrate the capacity to meet recurrent expenditure obligations. According to him, providing vehicles, uniforms and other equipment at the commencement of operations would be insufficient without sustainable arrangements for personnel salaries, professional training and operational maintenance. “Financial readiness is equally important. A state taking on policing must be able to sustain the service after the initial purchase of vehicles and uniforms. “Regular pay and continued training are essential to professional conduct. An institution that cannot meet its obligations to its officers becomes vulnerable to private patrons and unlawful demands on the public,” he cautioned. The Chief of Staff assured that federal policing would continue in states not yet financially or institutionally prepared to establish their own police services. Providing an update on the legislative process, Gbajabiamila confirmed that 24 State Houses of Assembly had approved the constitutional amendment providing for state police as at October 23, 2026 meeting the required two-thirds threshold. He disclosed that the Presidential Working Group had submitted the draft National Policing Bill and 29 consequential amendment bills to the Federal Ministry of Justice on October 19 for legislative review. According to him, after the review and the Working Group’s final consideration, the proposals would be presented to President Tinubu for approval before transmission to the National Assembly. He explained that the proposed framework would enable willing and capable states to assume greater responsibility for protecting their residents, while retaining a strong federal police institution to address interstate criminal activities and other specialised national security requirements. Gbajabiamila said the reform was intended to correct the structural imbalance under which state governments were responsible for responding to the consequences of insecurity without possessing corresponding authority to organise policing. “Bringing policing closer to the communities it serves can improve local intelligence and shorten the time between a call for help and an effective response,” he explained. Addressing concerns about the possible deployment of state police against political opponents, he assured Nigerians that the proposed legislation would contain enforceable safeguards, national professional standards and independent oversight mechanisms. “The concern that police powers could be used against political opponents or vulnerable communities is serious. Our answer is to place enforceable limits on those powers and provide remedies when they are abused. “A citizen’s entitlement to protection cannot depend on whom he supports or where she comes from,” the Chief of Staff declared. He said the framework had benefited from consultations with state governments, security institutions, members of the public and a Policy Advisory Committee drawn from the public and private sectors. Explaining why businesses should champion the reform, Gbajabiamila said insecurity affected investment decisions far beyond the immediate financial burden of hiring private security personnel. Said he: “The cost of the present arrangement is already in your accounts. You pay for additional security and disrupted deliveries. “You also bear losses that never appear as a separate charge: a factory expansion postponed, or a productive location excluded from your investment plans.” He argued that companies could not guarantee sustainable operations merely by securing their premises while surrounding communities remained unsafe. According to him: ‘A company can reinforce its perimeter. Its workers still have to travel home, and its suppliers still have to move through the surrounding communities. “Your long-term security depends on the strength of public institutions beyond your gates.” Turning to the administration’s wider security interventions, Gbajabiamila said President Tinubu had supported the modernisation of the Armed Forces through the induction of helicopters into Army Aviation and the restoration of more than 100 refurbished armoured fighting vehicles to active service. He recalled that the President commissioned three additional naval vessels in June to strengthen maritime security, noting that sustained operations against crude oil theft had contributed to improved oil production, foreign exchange earnings and government revenues. On food security, the Chief of Staff disclosed that the deployment of 10,000 Agro-Rangers across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory was helping to integrate agricultural production with security protection. He explained that the administration recognised that investments in improved seedlings, agricultural credit and other support programmes would achieve little without guaranteeing farmers’ access to their land. “Improved seedlings and access to credit will achieve little on farmland that its owners are afraid to cultivate. Protection makes those agricultural interventions usable,” he said. Gbajabiamila also highlighted the Presidential Forest Guards Initiative, under which more than 7,000 personnel drawn from seven frontline states had completed training by December 2025 to support security operations in areas exploited by criminal groups. He disclosed that President Tinubu had directed the preparation of a National Threat Assessment and a rolling five-year Strategic Defence Operations Plan in August to improve coordination, align security spending with operational priorities and strengthen institutional accountability. Acknowledging that Nigerians continued to face threats of kidnapping and violent attacks despite government investments in security, he said the administration recognised that its achievements must ultimately be measured by the safety of citizens. “Nigerians living with the threat of abduction or attack are entitled to judge us by their own safety. We recognise the distance between an improvement in national capacity and dependable protection in every community.” The Chief of Staff further linked the administration’s security interventions with its economic reform programme, including fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange restructuring and tax reforms. He acknowledged that the reforms had imposed considerable pressure on households and businesses but maintained that economic productivity and security were mutually dependent. “A government with inadequate revenues cannot sustain the institutions required to protect its citizens. An economy in which people cannot work safely cannot generate the revenues government needs. “We have therefore had to address both problems together, even as the costs of transition have placed considerable pressure on Nigerian households and businesses,” the Chief of Staff explained. Gbajabiamila urged investors to respond to improving security conditions by returning to communities where commercial activities had been disrupted, arguing that renewed investments would create employment, restore local supply chains and expand public revenues. He assured business leaders that the administration welcomed constructive criticism and practical recommendations, stressing that President Tinubu’s willingness to confront longstanding structural challenges required sustained cooperation from all stakeholders. “A farmer returning to his land and an employer reopening a business will be making decisions about their families’ futures. Our work together must give them sound reasons to proceed.” Founded on January 22, 1995, THISDAY is published by THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD., 35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria with offices in 36 states of Nigeria , the Federal Capital Territory and around the world. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.title_zh: 州警察：总统指示私营部门制定全面融资和实施方案
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/27/s.body_zh: 总统府已责成全国有组织私营部门为拟议中的州警察制度制定一套全面的融资与实施蓝图。总统府表示，企业必须积极参与建设维护投资、创造就业和增强经济韧性所需的安全机构。总统幕僚长兼国家警务法案总统工作组主席Femi Gbajabiamila阁下提出这一任务，并特别要求尼日利亚经济峰会组织（NESG）、商会和商业协会提出切实可行的融资方案、机构管理方案以及问责伙伴关系，以支持警务权力下放。他说，私营部门与改革成效直接相关，因为不安全状况已通过供应链中断、投资搁置、工厂扩建推迟和经济机会流失，给企业造成巨额成本。Gbajabiamila在阿布贾举行的第32届尼日利亚经济峰会“安全、稳定与经济韧性”全体会议上发言时表示，总统Bola Tinubu推动建立州警察，为企业直接参与建设支撑可持续经济增长的安全机构创造了机会。“因此，我请尼日利亚经济峰会组织把这项工作延伸到本次会议之外。认真提出私营部门关于州警察融资与实施的贡献意见，并就问责伙伴关系提出切实可行的建议。“将这项工作纳入立法进程，以及你们与州政府的沟通之中。就我们而言，我们仍负责把改革转化为公众可以信赖的保护措施。”他说。Gbajabiamila敦促商业领袖就拟议改革与州长和议员沟通，并提请他们关注有效的地方警务、创造就业与投资决策之间的关系。他解释称，企业管理机构、控制支出和评估风险的经验，可以强化新警务框架的设计与实施。他说，有组织私营部门还应提供安全失灵导致原本可行的投资无法推进的证据，使政策制定者能够确定哪里最迫切需要增加安全能力。“他的话是：“你们的参与还应提升改革的实质内容。随着立法进程推进，请审查有关融资和监督的各项建议。“请把你们管理机构和控制支出的经验带入讨论，帮助我们了解阻碍可行项目推进的安全失灵问题。”不过，这位幕僚长警告称，私营部门参与必须保持透明，绝不能损害警察机构的独立性。他说，企业可以在通信基础设施、设备维护和财务规划方面贡献专业知识，但此类伙伴关系必须在界限明确的法律和问责框架内运作。“凡是企业提供资源，这些投入都必须公布账目并接受独立审查。“公共资金必须保持稳定可靠，任何捐赠都绝不能换取对调查的影响力或优待待遇。目标是强化一项每位公民都能信赖的公共服务。”他警告道。Gbajabiamila表示，政府决心建立财政上可持续的州警察机构，并强调，希望运营自有警察服务的州必须证明其有能力承担经常性支出义务。他说，行动启动时提供车辆、制服和其他设备并不足够，还必须为人员薪资、专业培训和行动维护作出可持续安排。“财务准备同样重要。一个承担警务任务的州，必须能够在初步购置车辆和制服后继续维持该服务。“按时发放薪酬和持续培训是专业履职的必要条件。一个无法履行对警员义务的机构，会容易受到私人资助方控制以及非法公共要求的侵蚀。”他提醒道。这位幕僚长保证，对于尚未在财政或机构层面做好自建警察服务准备的州，联邦警务仍将继续运作。在介绍立法进程进展时，Gbajabiamila确认，截至2026年10月23日，已有24个州议会批准了关于设立州警察的宪法修正案，达到法定三分之二门槛。他透露，总统工作组已于10月19日向联邦司法部提交《国家警务法案》草案和29项配套修正案，供立法审议。他说，在完成审议和工作组最终审议后，这些提案将提交总统Tinubu批准，再送交国民议会。他解释称，拟议框架将使有意愿且有能力的州承担更多保护本州居民的责任，同时保留强大的联邦警察机构，以应对跨州犯罪活动和其他专业国家安全需求。Gbajabiamila说，这项改革旨在纠正一种结构性失衡，即州政府须应对不安全状况造成的后果，却无权组织警务。“让警务更贴近其服务的社区，可以改善地方情报工作，并缩短从求助到有效响应之间的时间。”他解释道。针对州警察可能被部署用于对付政治对手的担忧，他向尼日利亚人保证，拟议立法将包含可执行的保障措施、国家专业标准和独立监督机制。“警察权力可能被用于对付政治对手或弱势社区，这种担忧十分严肃。我们的应对办法是对这些权力设置可执行的限制，并在权力遭滥用时提供救济。“公民获得保护的权利不能取决于其支持谁或来自哪里。”这位幕僚长宣称。他说，该框架受益于与州政府、安全机构、公众成员以及由公共和私营部门人员组成的政策咨询委员会进行的磋商。Gbajabiamila解释企业为何应支持这项改革时表示，不安全状况对投资决策造成的影响，远远超出雇佣私人保安人员所带来的直接财务负担。他说：“现行安排的成本已经计入你们的账目。你们为额外安保和交付中断付费。“你们还承担从未作为单独费用出现的损失，例如工厂扩建推迟，或某个适宜生产的地点被排除在投资计划之外。”他论证称，如果周边社区仍不安全，企业仅靠保护自身场所无法保障持续运营。他说：“企业可以加强外围防护，但员工仍要回家，供应商仍要经过周边社区。“你们的长期安全取决于大门之外公共机构的力量。”谈及政府更广泛的安全干预措施时，Gbajabiamila表示，总统Tinubu支持通过将直升机列装陆军航空兵以及恢复100多辆经过翻新的装甲战斗车辆投入现役，推动武装部队现代化。他回忆称，总统于6月为其余3艘海军舰艇主持启用，以加强海上安全，并指出，针对原油盗取的持续行动已促进石油产量、外汇收入和政府财政收入增加。在粮食安全方面，这位幕僚长披露，政府已在19个州和联邦首都地区部署10,000名Agro-Rangers，以促进农业生产与安全保障相结合。他解释称，政府认识到，如果不保障农民能够进入自己的土地，对改良种子、农业信贷和其他支持计划的投入将难有成效。“在土地所有者因害怕而不敢耕种的农田上，改良种子和信贷获取都难以发挥作用。安全保障才能使这些农业干预措施真正落地。”Gbajabiamila还强调总统森林守卫倡议，根据该倡议，截至2025年12月，来自7个前线州的7,000多名人员已完成训练，以支持在犯罪团伙活动地区的安全行动。他透露，总统Tinubu已于8月指示编制《国家威胁评估》和滚动五年期《战略防务行动计划》，以改善协调工作、使安全支出与行动重点保持一致，并强化机构问责。Gbajabiamila承认，尽管政府不断增加安全投入，尼日利亚人仍持续面临绑架和暴力袭击威胁，但他表示，政府认识到，其成效最终必须以公民安全来衡量。“生活在绑架或袭击威胁中的尼日利亚人，有权依据自身安全状况评价我们。我们认识到，国家能力提升与每个社区都获得可靠保护之间仍有差距。”这位幕僚长进一步将政府的安全干预与其经济改革计划联系起来，包括取消燃油补贴、外汇结构调整和税收改革。他承认，这些改革给家庭和企业带来了相当大的压力，但坚持认为，经济生产率与安全相互依存。“收入不足的政府无法维持保护公民所需的机构。在人们无法安全工作的情况下，经济也无法创造政府所需的收入。“因此，我们不得不同时处理这两个问题，尽管转型成本已对尼日利亚家庭和企业造成相当大的压力。”这位幕僚长解释道。Gbajabiamila敦促投资者因安全状况改善而重返那些商业活动曾受干扰的地区，并认为，恢复投资将创造就业、恢复本地供应链并扩大公共收入。他向商业领袖保证，政府欢迎建设性批评和切实可行的建议，并强调，总统Tinubu正视长期结构性挑战的意愿，需要所有利益相关方持续合作。“返乡的农民和重新开业的雇主将在为家人的未来作出决定。我们共同的努力必须给他们充分理由继续前进。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，社址位于尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都地区以及世界各地设有办公室。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，通过全平台面向政治、商业、专业和外交精英及更广泛的中产阶级报道，同时为有抱负者和千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇平台。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title: Dangote Refinery’s historic IPO nets investors from 120 countries worldwide, 54 in Africa
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.summary_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其里程碑式首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自全球六个有人居住大洲120个国家的投资者申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has successfully concluded its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO), attracting investor applications from 120 countries across all six inhabited continents, including all 54 African countries. In a statement on Tuesday, the company described the development as an unprecedented demonstration of the continent’s capacity to mobilise capital and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. The historic offering, widely described as The People’s IPO, achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, bringing together investors from across the continent and beyond in a transaction that could redefine the scale, accessibility and international reach of African capital markets. More than a conventional fundraising exercise, the IPO has become a landmark in financial inclusion, showing how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions, and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants. The transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation. For Dangote Industries Limited, the IPO’s conclusion marks a defining moment in its industrial journey, shifting the refinery’s ownership proposition from an investment driven by a single entrepreneurial vision to an opportunity for broader African participation. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise, and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development. “When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries. “To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It shows our people don’t just want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it, and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said. “We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. We built the refinery in Africa, through African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. “Today, we have made history together. But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs, and industrialists that this transaction inspires. Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny. As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it.” The statement said the IPO’s geographical reach is particularly significant for a continent where capital markets have historically been fragmented by national boundaries, differing regulatory environments and limited retail investor participation. By attracting applications from all 54 African countries, the transaction has shown the potential for a more connected investment ecosystem, allowing Africans to participate in major industrial opportunities beyond their domestic markets. The offering also highlights the growing importance of digital financial infrastructure in widening investment access. Through partnerships involving traditional financial institutions and technology-driven investment platforms, the transaction created multiple channels for eligible investors to express interest and submit applications. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects. “The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications from 120 countries demonstrate extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence investors place in this refinery’s future. We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said. “What makes this transaction particularly meaningful is the breadth of participation. The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents. That is a powerful endorsement of the refinery’s potential and of Africa’s growing relevance in global investment markets.” The refinery’s IPO opened on 14 September, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on 13 October, the offer was extended to 27 October after the Securities and Exchange Commission approved it, giving investors across Africa and other international markets more time to participate. The extension reflected the Group’s stated ambition to prioritise broad ownership alongside the transaction’s financial objectives. Beyond the refinery’s industrial significance, the IPO also established a model for collaboration across Africa’s financial services ecosystem. Its distribution network brought together institutions across banking, securities trading, financial technology, and investor engagement, showing how coordinated infrastructure can expand access to large-scale investment opportunities. Dangote Industries Limited Group Chief Financial Officer Murat Erden said the transaction set an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets, speaking to the offering’s execution and broader significance. “The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets. Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the continent’s growing appetite for investment. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said. “Importantly, this transaction is underpinned by exceptional industrial and financial fundamentals. With US$22.5 billion in revenue and US$5.52 billion in EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, Dangote Refinery combines world-class industrial scale, strong profitability and significant long-term growth potential. Our greatest achievement is not simply the capital we mobilise, but the doors we open and the foundation we lay for future generations of African investors, entrepreneurs and businesses. We believe the People’s IPO will be remembered not only as a landmark transaction in African capital market history, but also as a blueprint for a more inclusive, interconnected and globally competitive African financial ecosystem — one in which Africans increasingly finance, own and share in the prosperity created by their continent’s industrial transformation.” The successful conclusion of the offer comes as Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals pursues an ambitious programme to expand its refining and petrochemical operations, strengthen its distribution network and support greater energy security across Africa. Located in Lagos, the refinery represents one of the continent’s largest private industrial investments and a major effort to reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products while building domestic processing capacity
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: Dangote炼油厂历史性首次公开募股吸引全球120个国家的投资者，其中54个来自非洲
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 丹格特炼油与石化公司已成功完成其具有里程碑意义的首次公开募股（IPO），吸引了来自六大有人居住洲120个国家的投资者申购申请，其中包括非洲全部54个国家。该公司周二发表声明称，这一进展前所未有地展现了非洲大陆调动资本、扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。此次历史性发行被广泛称为“人民IPO”，实现了对非洲100%的地域覆盖，将非洲各地乃至海外投资者汇聚到一起完成交易，可能重新定义非洲资本市场的规模、可及性和国际影响力。这次IPO不只是传统的融资活动，更成为金融普惠的里程碑，展示了数字技术、协同配合的金融机构以及创新分销渠道如何将数百万潜在投资者与过去主要由机构投资者和高净值人士主导的投资机会连接起来。此次交易得到了广泛商业银行、证券经纪公司、金融科技平台、资本市场机构和分销合作伙伴网络的支持，各方协作突破了国界限制、扩大了本次发行的参与范围，并为散户参与开辟了新路径。对丹格特集团有限公司而言，IPO的完成标志着其工业发展历程中的决定性时刻，使该炼油厂的所有权模式从依靠单一企业家愿景推动的投资，转变为更广泛的非洲投资者共同参与的机会。丹格特集团有限公司总裁兼首席执行官阿里科·丹格特表示，这一成果有力印证了非洲的信心、进取精神以及调动自身资源推动发展的能力。“当初我们着手建设这座炼油厂时，许多人怀疑如此规模的项目能否由非洲人建成。我们证明了非洲能够建设它。如今，通过这次历史性IPO，我们展示了一项同样重要的事实：非洲人已经准备好拥有并参与自身产业所创造的繁荣。“来自非洲全部54个国家的投资者提交申购申请，对我而言意义重大。这表明我们的人民不只想消费非洲生产的产品，还愿意投资并拥有这些产业，分享其未来。这就是我们始终坚信的非洲。”他说。“我们推动这次IPO并非仅仅因为需要筹集资本。我们希望打开所有权的大门，让普通非洲人有机会参与一家具有全球意义的企业，并建立一种共享繁荣的新文化。我们依靠非洲人的决心在非洲建设了这座炼油厂，它的未来也必须为非洲人创造机会。“今天，我们共同创造了历史。但更大的成就，将是这次交易激励起来的非洲投资者、创业者和实业家群体。我们的目标不只是打造成功的企业，还要帮助建设一个繁荣、自给自足的非洲，使非洲人民成为其经济命运的参与者。随着我们推进扩张计划和“2030愿景”战略，我们将继续专注于提升运营表现，深化对非洲能源安全的贡献，并打造一家能够回报投资者信任的企业。”声明称，这次IPO的地域覆盖范围尤其重要，因为非洲大陆的资本市场历来受到国界分割、监管环境差异以及散户参与度有限等因素影响。通过吸引非洲全部54个国家提交申购申请，此次交易展示了一个更加互联的投资生态所具有的潜力，使非洲人能够参与本国市场之外的重要工业投资机会。此次发行还凸显了数字金融基础设施在扩大投资可及性方面日益重要的作用。通过传统金融机构与技术驱动型投资平台之间的合作，此次交易为符合条件的投资者提供了多种表达投资意愿并提交申购申请的渠道。丹格特炼油与石化公司董事总经理兼首席执行官戴维·伯德表示，国际市场反响反映出投资者对该炼油厂运营能力、工业规模及长期增长前景的信心。“这次IPO成功完成，是丹格特炼油与石化公司的重要里程碑。来自120个国家的投资者申购申请证明，国际社会对我们的业务展现出非凡兴趣，也体现了投资者对这家炼油厂未来的信心。我们已经建成全球最具规模的炼油与石化综合体之一，当前重点仍是将这种工业规模转化为卓越运营、可持续增长和长期股东价值。”他说。“让此次交易更具意义的是广泛参与。投资者遍布非洲每一个国家以及六大有人居住洲，并有机会持有一家重要非洲工业企业的股份。这是对该炼油厂潜力以及非洲在全球投资市场中日益提升重要性的有力背书。”该炼油厂的IPO于9月14日开放认购，以每股525奈拉的价格发行41亿股普通股，拟募集资金约2.15万亿奈拉。此次发行原定于10月13日结束，但在证券交易委员会批准后延长至10月27日，为非洲及其他国际市场的投资者提供了更多参与时间。延长期限体现了集团在追求交易财务目标的同时，优先推动广泛所有权的既定愿景。除炼油厂本身的重要工业意义外，此次IPO还为非洲金融服务生态体系内的协作建立了范例。其分销网络将银行、证券交易、金融科技和投资者互动等领域的机构汇聚起来，展示了协同基础设施如何扩大公众参与大规模投资机会。丹格特集团有限公司首席财务官穆拉特·尔登表示，这次交易为非洲大陆资本市场树立了重要先例，其执行过程和广泛意义同样值得关注。“丹格特炼油厂人民IPO远不只是一次具有里程碑意义的融资活动。它标志着非洲资本市场演进过程中的决定性时刻，展现了我们大陆调动国内储蓄、连接跨境投资者以及扩大战略工业资产所有权覆盖范围的能力。投资者覆盖120个国家，包括非洲全部54个国家，这是一项非凡成就，也是非洲大陆投资意愿日益增强的有力证明。通过汇聚银行、资本市场机构、证券经纪商、金融科技平台和创新的数字分销渠道，我们证明了非洲资本市场能够跨越国界，让数百万人获得过去难以触及的投资机会。”他说。“尤为重要的是，这次交易建立在卓越的工业和财务基本面之上。2026年前九个月，丹格特炼油厂实现225亿美元收入和55.2亿美元EBITDA，兼具世界级工业规模、强劲盈利能力及显著的长期增长潜力。我们最大的成就不仅是调动资本，更是打开大门，为未来几代非洲投资者、创业者和企业奠定基础。我们相信，人民IPO不仅会作为非洲资本市场史上的里程碑交易被铭记，也将成为建设更具包容性、更互联且具备全球竞争力的非洲金融生态的蓝图。在这个生态中，非洲人将越来越多地为自身大陆的工业转型提供资金、拥有产业，并分享其创造的繁荣。”此次发行成功完成之际，丹格特炼油与石化公司正推进一项雄心勃勃的计划，以扩大炼油和石化业务、加强分销网络，并支持提升非洲整体能源安全。该炼油厂位于拉各斯，是非洲大陆规模最大的私人工业投资之一，也是非洲为减少对进口成品油依赖、建设本土加工能力所作的重大努力。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/kano.body: The Kano State House of Assembly has approved the proposed constitutional amendment to allow state governments to establish and operate their own police forces. The approval was confirmed by the Majority Leader of the Assembly, Lawan Hussaini Dala, shortly after plenary on Tuesday. Dala said the lawmakers had considered and approved the proposed constitutional review to provide for the establishment of state police. “We have approved the constitutional review for the establishment of state police at plenary today,” he said. The approval followed deliberations on the proposed amendments to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which seek to give state governments the legal authority to establish and operate their own police forces. During plenary, the lawmakers considered the constitutional alteration bill in the Committee of the Whole, deliberating on clauses one to 26 of the proposed amendment. The lawmakers had earlier adopted a motion to consider the constitutional amendment bill in the Committee of the Whole before proceeding with deliberations on its provisions. https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 举着红旗的农民从伊加特普里出发，沿纳西克—孟买公路向孟买行进。傍晚， Fadnavis会见了由阿吉特·纳瓦莱带领的农民代表团。 Maharashtra首席部长德夫德拉· Fadnavis向农民保证，州政府将提供一切可能的援助，帮助他们克服当前干旱状况带来的挑战。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: The farmers carrying red flags began their march from Igatpuri to Mumbai along the Nashik–Mumbai highway. All India Kisan Sabha leader Ajit Nawale called for reform in the farm loan waiver policy. He argued that farmers who regularly repay their loans should benefit from the scheme. In the evening, Fadnavis met a delegation of farmers under the leadership of Ajit Nawale. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has assured farmers that the state government will extend all possible assistance to help them overcome the challenges arising from the prevailing drought conditions. Fadnavis emphasised that the government was committed to reducing the hardships faced by farming families through financial assistance, drinking water arrangements, fodder supplies and measures to strengthen agricultural support systems. The Chief Minister announced that pending instalments under the Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana would be paid to eligible farmers. He also assured that the government will consider demand for increasing the ₹ 50,000 incentive provided to farmers who regularly repay their crop loans. "A ministerial group constituted to examine farm loan waivers will discuss the proposal to increase the incentive. A suitable decision will be taken after considering the state's financial position," said Fadnavis. Fadnavis also ordered officials to expedite the release of pending instalments under the Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana for women beneficiaries who have completed their e-KYC verification. The Chief Minister said Maharashtra was among the leading states in terms of the number of women receiving benefits under such welfare schemes. The Chief Minister directed the concerned department to examine the possibility of restoring the triggers previously used under the crop insurance scheme. The state government has expressed a positive view on increasing the monthly honorarium of school nutrition programme workers. These workers currently receive ₹ 2,500 per month, and the proposal under consideration would raise their honorarium by ₹ 1,000 to ₹ 3,500 per month. After the assurance, Ajit Nawale announced the decision to withdraw Long March. "CM Fadnavis responded positively to our demands. So we have decided to withdraw the Long March." said Nawale. The meeting was attended by Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Water Resources Minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan, Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne and MLA Vinod Nikole

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 举着红旗的农民从伊加特普里出发，沿纳西克—孟买公路向孟买行进。全印度农民协会领导人阿杰特·纳瓦勒呼吁改革农业贷款减免政策。他认为 regularly 偿还贷款的农民应当从该计划中受益。傍晚，法德纳维斯会见了由阿杰特·纳瓦勒带领的农民代表团。马哈拉施特拉邦首席部长德文德拉·法德纳维斯向农民保证，邦政府将提供一切可能的援助，帮助他们克服当前干旱状况带来的挑战。法德纳维斯强调，政府致力于通过财政援助、饮用水供应、饲料供应以及加强农业支持体系的措施，减轻农业家庭面临的困难。首席部长宣布，符合条件的农民将获得“Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana”计划下待发放的款项。他还保证，政府将考虑提高向 regularly 偿还作物贷款农民提供的 ₹ 50,000 奖励金额。“为研究农业贷款减免而成立的部长级小组将讨论提高奖励金额的提议。在考虑邦财政状况后，将作出适当决定。”法德纳维斯说。法德纳维斯还命令官员加快向已完成电子身份验证的女性受益人发放“Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana”计划下的待拨款项。首席部长表示，马哈拉施特拉邦是此类福利计划女性受益人数最多的邦之一。首席部长指示相关部门研究恢复此前在农作物保险计划中使用的触发条件。邦政府对提高学校营养计划工作人员的月度酬金持积极态度。这些工作人员目前每月获得 ₹ 2,500，正在考虑的提议将把其酬金提高 ₹ 1,000，达到每月 ₹ 3,500。在获得保证后，阿杰特·纳瓦勒宣布撤回长march行动。“首席部长法德纳维斯积极回应了我们的要求。因此，我们决定撤回长march行动。”纳瓦勒说。出席会议的还有副首席部长埃克纳特·辛德、努内特拉·阿杰特·帕瓦尔，水资源部长拉德哈克里希纳·维赫·帕蒂尔、水资源部长吉里什·马哈詹、财政部长钱德拉谢卡尔·巴万库勒、农业部长达塔特雷·巴尔内以及议员维诺德·尼科莱

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.summary: Layer 1 The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.summary_zh: 据美国国务院消息，美国已将50个国家的公民列入名单。这些公民申请某些访问签证时，必须缴纳最高20,000美元的签证保证金，尼日利亚位列其中。国务院在2026年10月2日发布的通知中列出了适用签证保证金计划的国家及其各自实施日期。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.body: Layer 1 The United States has listed 50 countries whose citizens must pay a visa bond of up to $20,000 when applying for certain visitor visas, including Nigeria, according to the US Department of State. The measure applies to eligible applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas travelling on passports issued by the listed countries. The bond amounts are $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000, with the specific amount determined by a consular officer during the visa interview. In a notice published on October 2, 2026, the Department of State outlined the countries subject to the visa bond programme and their respective implementation dates. The programme operates under Section 221(g)(3) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, with the department stating that the requirement applies regardless of where an applicant submits their visa application. The 50 countries listed by the US Department of State, alongside their implementation dates, are: Nigerian citizens applying for B-1 business or B-2 tourist visas may be required to post a bond of $10,000, $15,000 or $20,000 if they are otherwise eligible for the visa. The amount is determined during the visa interview. The bond is an additional financial requirement and does not guarantee that the applicant will receive a visa. Applicants must submit Department of Homeland Security Form I-352 and agree to the bond’s terms through the US Department of the Treasury’s Pay.gov platform. The department warns applicants not to pay a bond before being instructed to do so by a consular officer. Applicants are expected to use the specific payment link supplied through official instructions. The bond may be paid by the applicant or a third party, such as a relative, friend or business associate. However, the name of the person identified as the bond obligor on Form I-352 must match the name of the person making the payment. If the bond conditions are satisfied, the money is refundable under the programme’s terms. The programme also imposes travel conditions on people who post visa bonds. According to the State Department, bond holders must enter and leave the United States through designated commercial air ports of entry, including US Customs and Border Protection preclearance locations. They are not permitted to use charter aircraft, general aviation, land borders or sea ports of entry under the stated bond conditions. Failure to comply with the designated entry and exit requirements could result in problems with entry or the recording of a traveller’s departure. The department outlined several circumstances under which a bond may be cancelled and the deposit returned automatically. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.title_zh: 美国签证保证金：包括尼日利亚在内的完整国家名单及最高2万美元缴费规定
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/us-v.body_zh:
第一层：美国国务院表示，美国已列出50个国家，其公民申请特定访问签证时须缴纳最高20,000美元的签证保证金，其中包括尼日利亚。

这项措施适用于持有所列国家签发的护照、申请B-1商务签证或B-2旅游签证且符合资格的申请人。

保证金金额为10,000美元、15,000美元或20,000美元，具体金额由领事官员在签证面谈期间确定。

美国国务院在2026年10月2日发布的通知中列出了适用签证保证金计划的国家及其各自的实施日期。

该计划依据《移民和国籍法》第221(g)(3)条实施。国务院表示，无论申请人在何处递交签证申请，均须遵守这一要求。

美国国务院列出的50个国家及其实施日期如下：

尼日利亚公民申请B-1商务签证或B-2旅游签证时，如符合签证的其他资格条件，可能须缴纳10,000美元、15,000美元或20,000美元的保证金。

具体金额将在签证面谈期间确定。

保证金是一项额外的财务要求，并不保证申请人一定获发签证。

申请人必须提交美国国土安全部I-352表格，并通过美国财政部的Pay.gov平台同意保证金条款。

国务院提醒申请人，在领事官员指示缴纳保证金之前不得付款。

申请人应使用官方指引提供的专用付款链接。

保证金可由申请人本人或亲属、朋友、商业伙伴等第三方支付。

但是，I-352表格中被列为保证金义务人的姓名必须与付款人的姓名一致。

如果满足保证金条件，款项可依照该计划的规定退还。

该计划还对缴纳签证保证金的人施加旅行条件。

据国务院称，保证金缴纳者必须从指定的商业航空入境口岸入境并离境，包括美国海关与边境保护局预先清关地点。

根据规定的保证金条件，他们不得使用包机、一般航空、陆路边境或海港入境口岸。

未遵守指定入境和离境要求可能导致入境受阻，或影响旅行者离境记录的登记。

国务院列举了若干可以取消保证金并自动退还押金的情形。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.title: Lawmakers move to make formal identification compulsory for renting apartments in Abuja
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary: The Senate on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, to present valid means of identification before renting apartments as part of efforts to curb criminal activities.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.summary_zh: 参议院周二决定启动立法，要求联邦首都 Territory（FCT）阿布贾的租户在租赁公寓前出示有效身份证件，以协助遏制犯罪活动。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/more.body: The Senate on Tuesday resolved to initiate legislation requiring tenants in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, to present valid means of identification before renting apartments as part of efforts to curb criminal activities. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio , directed the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, to draft the bill for consideration by the National Assembly. Mr Akpabio gave the directive during the plenary while lawmakers were debating a report by the Senate committees on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations; Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters; Foreign Affairs; and Special Duties on the need to protect Nigerians from being trafficked to Libya for slavery. The report was presented by Aniekan Bassey, chair of the Senate Committee on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations. Mr Akpabio expressed concern that many property owners rent out their properties to strangers without obtaining adequate information about their identities, occupations and other relevant details. He argued that the lack of proper documentation makes it difficult for security agencies to trace suspects when crimes are committed, allowing perpetrators to escape without leaving a clear trail. “A lot of people just give their properties to strangers. They don’t even have any papers to know where they come from. In some instances, the phone number that is used in renting the property does not even belong to the occupant of the house. So when something happens, the person will escape and then leave no trace,” he said. The Senate President urged Mr Bamidele to consider legislation that would strengthen tenancy regulations and make landlords more accountable for verifying prospective tenants’ identities. “People enter people’s properties with very nefarious intentions and, at the end of the day, they will just commit some crimes, traffic people’s children and make money while living in the house itself. It is something that we must tighten the laws on tenancy,” he said. Mr Akpabio proposed adopting an approach similar to the banking sector’s Know Your Customer (KYC) policy, which requires financial institutions to verify customers’ identities. “As you know in the bank, they say, know your customer; this one we can say, know your tenants. Let’s make the necessary law for the FCT, for instance. We can enact an Act for the FCT that says know your tenants so that nobody will come and live in the house and perpetrate crime,” he said. He said the proposed legislation could also cover the rental of shops and other commercial spaces, arguing that inadequate identity verification could expose occupants and business owners to criminal attacks. Mr Akpabio said people renting shops should provide verifiable identification, including a driver’s licence or international passport, to help security agencies trace them if they are implicated in criminal activities. He said the lack of reliable tenant information could leave property owners unable to identify or help locate people who used their premises to commit crimes. “And then even those that are going to do shoplets, we can use that opportunity to regulate shoplets because people go into secluded environments and then do shoplets, and then they move in and they rob them in the night and escape. To support his argument, Mr Akpabio recalled measures his administration introduced to tackle kidnapping when he was governor of Akwa Ibom State. He said his government prescribed the death penalty for kidnapping and introduced measures involving the destruction of property used as hideouts by criminals. The Senate President noted that the measures encouraged landlords to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious behaviour for fear of losing them. He said similar measures could help deter criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as bases for criminal activities. If enacted as envisaged by the Senate President, the proposed legislation would require landlords in the FCT to verify prospective tenants’ identities before letting out their property. The proposal is intended to help security agencies trace people suspected of committing crimes from their residential addresses and discourage criminals from using rented apartments and commercial premises as hideouts. However, its effectiveness would depend on the legislation’s details, including how identities would be verified, what records landlords would be required to keep, and how compliance would be monitored. If enacted, the law could make it easier for investigators to establish the identities of tenants linked to rented property. It could also impose additional responsibilities on landlords and property agents, potentially requiring them to retain identification records and provide relevant information to authorised authorities when legally required. The proposal could, however, raise concerns about privacy, the security of tenants’ personal information and the possibility of landlords using the requirement to discriminate against prospective tenants or deny accommodation to people who cannot readily provide the prescribed documents. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 provides a framework for lawful, secure handling of personal information. Any system requiring landlords to collect and retain tenants’ identification details would need to comply with applicable data protection obligations. The proposal remains in the drafting stage, based on the proceedings described by the Senate President. It would need to go through the legislative process before becoming law
